1.1: The words of Yirmeyahu the son of Ḥilqiyahu, of the kohenim who were in Anathoth in the land of Binyamin,
1.2: to whom the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came in the days of Yoshiyahu son of Amon, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
1.3: And it came in the days of Yahoyaqim, son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, until the end of the eleventh year of Tsiḏqiyahu, son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, until the exile of Yerushalayim in the fifth month.
1.4: Now the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
1.5: “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I qadosh you - I appointed you a naḇi to nations.”
1.6: And I said, “Ah, Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! See, I do not know how to speak, for I am a youth.”
1.7: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am a youth,’ but go to all to whom I send you, and speak whatever I command you.
1.8: “Do not fear their faces, for I am with you to deliver you,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.9: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 put forth His hand and touched my mouth, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “See, I have put My words in your mouth.
1.10: “See, I have this day appointed you over the nations and over the reigns, to root out and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.”
1.11: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying, “What do you see, Yirmeyahu?” And I said, “I see a branch of an almond tree.”
1.12: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “You have seen well, for I am watching over My word to do it.”
1.13: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me a second time, saying, “What do you see?” And I said, “I see a boiling pot, and it is facing from the north.”
1.14: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Out of the north evil is let loose on all the inhabitants of the land.
1.15: “For look, I am calling all the clans of the reigns of the north,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “And they shall come and each one put his throne at the entrance of the gates of Yerushalayim, against all its walls all around, and against all the cities of Yahuḏah.
1.16: “And I shall pronounce My judgments against them concerning all their evil, because they have forsaken Me, burned incense to other mighty ones, and bowed themselves to the works of their own hands.
1.17: “Now, gird up your loins and arise, and speak to them all that I command you. Do not break down before their faces, lest I break you before them.
1.18: “For look, I have made you this day a walled city and an iron column, and bronze walls against all the land, against the melaḵim of Yahuḏah, against her heads, against her kohenim, and against the people of the land.
1.19: “And they shall fight against you, but not prevail against you. For I am with you,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “to deliver you.”

10.1: Hear the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 speaks to you, O house of Yisra’ĕl.
10.2: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Do not learn the way of the gentiles, and do not be frightened by the signs of the shamayim, for the gentiles are frightened by them.
10.3: “For the prescribed customs of these peoples are worthless, for one cuts a tree from the forest, work for the hands of a craftsman with a cutting tool.
10.4: “They adorn it with silver and gold, they fasten it with nails and hammers so that it does not topple.
10.5: “They are like a rounded post, and they do not speak. They have to be carried, because they do not walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they do no evil, nor is it in them to do any good.”
10.6: There is none like You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. You are great, and great is Your Name in might.
10.7: Who would not revere You, O Meleḵ of the nations? For this is Your due, for among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their malḵuth, there is none like You.
10.8: They are both brutish and foolish, an instruction of worthlessness is the tree.
10.9: Silver is beaten into plates; it is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the craftsman and of the hands of the smith; draped in blue and purple; all of them are the work of skilled ones.
10.10: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is truly Elohim. He is the living Elohim and the everlasting Meleḵ. At His wrath the earth shakes, and nations are unable to stand His displeasure.
10.11: Say to them this, “The elah that did not make the shamayim and the earth shall perish from the earth and from under these shamayim.”
10.12: He has made the earth by His power, He has established the world by His wisdom, and has stretched out the shamayim by His understanding.
10.13: When He makes His voice heard, there is a roaring of waters in the shamayim. And He makes vapors rise from the ends of the earth. The lightnings for rain He has made, and brings wind from His treasuries.
10.14: Everyone is brutish in knowledge; every smith is put to shame by his idol. For his molded image is falsehood, and there is no spirit in them.
10.15: They are worthless, a work of mockery. In the time of their punishment they perish.
10.16: The Portion of Ya’aqoḇ is not like these, for He is the Maker of all, and Yisra’ĕl is the tribe of His inheritance - 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts is His Name.
10.17: Gather up your bundle from the ground, you who live under siege!
10.18: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, at this time I am hurling out the inhabitants of the land, and shall distress them, so that they feel it.”
10.19: Woe to me for my breaking! My wound is grievous, but I say, “This is my sickness, and I bear it.
10.20: “My tent has been ravaged, and all my cords have been broken. My children have gone from me, and they are no more. There is no one to pitch my tent any more, or to put up my curtains.
10.21: For the shepherds have become brutish, and they have not sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Therefore they did not understand, and all their flock scattered.”
10.22: See, it has come, the voice of a report, and a great shaking out of the land of the north, to make the cities of Yahuḏah a waste, a habitation of jackals.
10.23: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I know the way of man is not in himself, it is not for man who walks to direct his own steps.
10.24: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, chastise me, but with right-ruling - not in Your displeasure, lest You bring me to naught.
10.25: Pour out Your wrath on the gentiles who do not know You, and on the tribes who do not call on Your Name. For they have eaten up Ya’aqoḇ, devoured him and consumed him, and laid waste his home.

11.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
11.2: “Hear the words of this Covenant, and speak to the men of Yahuḏah and to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
11.3: “And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this Covenant,
11.4: which I commanded your fathers in the day when I brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the iron furnace, saying, ‘Obey My voice, and you shall do according to all that I command you, and you shall be My people, and I be your Elohim,’
11.5: in order to establish the oath which I have sworn to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.” ’ ” And I answered and said, “Amĕn, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
11.6: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Yahuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, saying, ‘Hear the words of this Covenant and do them.
11.7: ‘For I earnestly warned your fathers in the day that I brought them up out of the land of Mitsrayim, until this day, rising early and warning, saying, “Obey My voice.”
11.8: ‘But they did not obey or incline their ear, but everyone walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought on them all the words of this Covenant, which I commanded them to do, and they did not do.’ ”
11.9: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “There is a conspiracy among the men of Yahuḏah and among the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
11.10: “They have turned back to the wickednesses of their forefathers who refused to hear My Words, and they have gone after other mighty ones to serve them. The house of Yisra’ĕl and the house of Yahuḏah have broken My Covenant I made with their fathers.”
11.11: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am bringing evil on them which they are unable to escape. Then they shall cry out to Me, but I shall not listen to them.
11.12: “And the cities of Yahuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim shall go and cry out to the mighty ones to whom they burn incense, but they shall bring no deliverance to them at all in the time of their evil.
11.13: “For your mighty ones have become as many as your cities, O Yahuḏah. And you have put up as many altars to shame as there are streets in Yerushalayim - altars to burn incense to Ba’al.
11.14: “And you, do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or prayer for them, for I do not hear them in the time that they cry out to Me because of their evil.
11.15: “Why should My beloved be in My house - she has done wickedness with many. And does the qodesh flesh remove your evil from you? Then you rejoice?
11.16: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has named you, ‘Green Olive Tree, Lovely, of Pleasant Fruit.’ With the noise of a great sound He has lit it on fire, and its branches shall be broken.
11.17: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, who planted you, has spoken evil against you for the evil of the house of Yisra’ĕl and of the house of Yahuḏah, which they have done against themselves to provoke Me, by burning incense to Ba’al.”
11.18: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made it known to me, and I know it. Then You showed me their deeds.
11.19: But I was like a gentle lamb brought to the slaughter. And I did not know that they had plotted against me, saying, “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more.”
11.20: But, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, who judges righteously, who tries kidneys and heart, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for unto You I have revealed my cause.
11.21: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning the men of Anathoth who are seeking your life, saying, ‘Do not naḇa in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, lest you die by our hand’ -
11.22: therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, ‘See, I am punishing them, the young men shall die by the sword, their sons and their daughters shall die by scarcity of food.
11.23: ‘And there shall be no remnant of them, for I bring evil on the men of Anathoth - the year of their punishment.’ ”

12.1: Righteous are You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, when I plead with You. Indeed, let me speak with You about right-rulings. Why has the way of the wicked prospered? All the workers of treachery are at ease?
12.2: You have planted them and they have taken root, they grow and they bear fruit. You are near in their mouth but far from their kidneys.
12.3: But You have known me, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. You see me, and You have tried my heart toward You. Draw them away like sheep for slaughter, and qadosh them for the day of slaughter.
12.4: How long shall the land mourn, and the plants of every field wither? The beasts and birds are consumed, for the evil of those who dwell there, because they said, “He does not see our latter ending.”
12.5: “If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how do you contend with horses? And if in the land of peace, you feel safe, then how do you manage in the pride of the Yardĕn?
12.6: “For even your brothers, the house of your father, even they have betrayed you, even they have cried aloud after you. Do not believe them, even though they speak smooth words to you.
12.7: “I have forsaken My house, I have left My inheritance, I have given the beloved of My being into the hand of her enemies.
12.8: “My inheritance has become to Me like a lion in the forest. It cries out against Me, therefore I have hated it.
12.9: “My inheritance is to Me like a speckled bird of prey, the birds of prey all around are against her. Go, gather all the beasts of the field, bring them to devour!
12.10: “Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard, they have trodden My portion under foot, they have made My pleasant portion become a deserted wilderness.
12.11: “They have laid it waste - a waste, it mourns to Me. All the land is laid waste, because no one takes it to heart.
12.12: “The ravagers have come on all the bare heights in the wilderness, for the sword of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is devouring from one end of the land to the other end of the land. There is no peace to any flesh.
12.13: “They have sown wheat but reaped thorns, they have exhausted themselves - they do not profit. And they shall be ashamed of your harvest because of the burning displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
12.14: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “As for all My evil neighbors who touch the inheritance which I have caused My people Yisra’ĕl to inherit; see, I am plucking them out of their land, and I shall pluck out the house of Yahuḏah from their midst.
12.15: “And it shall be, after My plucking them out, I shall return, and have compassion on them and bring them back, everyone to his inheritance and everyone to his land.
12.16: “And it shall be, if they learn well the Ways of My people, to swear by My Name, ‘As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives,’ as they taught My people to swear by Ba’al, then they shall be established in the midst of My people.
12.17: “But if they do not obey, I shall pluck up, pluck up and destroy that nation,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

13.1: Thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Go and get yourself a linen girdle, and put it on your loins, but do not put it in water.”
13.2: So I bought a girdle according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and put it on my loins.
13.3: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me the second time, saying,
13.4: “Take the girdle that you have bought, which is on your loins, and arise, go to Perath, and hide it there in a hole in the rock.”
13.5: And I went and hid it by Perath, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded me.
13.6: And it came to be after many days that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Arise, go to Perath, and take from there the girdle which I commanded you to hide there.”
13.7: So I went to Perath and dug, and I took the girdle from the place where I had hidden it. And there was the girdle, ruined. It was completely useless.
13.8: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
13.9: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Thus I ruin the pride of Yahuḏah and the great pride of Yerushalayim.
13.10: ‘This evil people, who refuse to hear My Words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart, and walk after other mighty ones to serve them and to bow themselves to them, is like this girdle which is completely useless.
13.11: ‘For as the girdle clings to the loins of a man, so I have caused all the house of Yisra’ĕl and all the house of Yahuḏah to cling to Me,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘to become Mine - for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for an adorning. But they did not listen.’
13.12: “And you shall speak to them this word, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Every pitcher is to be filled with wine.” ’ And when they say to you, ‘Do we not know that every pitcher should be filled with wine?’
13.13: “Then say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am filling all the inhabitants of this land, and the melaḵim who sit on the throne of Dawiḏ, and the kohenim, and the neḇi’im, and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim with drunkenness!
13.14: “And I shall dash them one against another, both the fathers and the sons together,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “I do not spare nor pardon nor have compassion, that I should not destroy them.” ’ ”
13.15: Listen and give ear, do not be proud, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken.
13.16: Give esteem to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim before He brings darkness, and before your feet stumble on the dark mountains, and while you are looking for light, He turns it into the shadow of death, makes it dense darkness.
13.17: And if you do not listen, my being shall weep in secret for your pride, and my eyes bitterly weep and run down with tears, because the flock of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be taken captive.
13.18: Say to the meleḵ and to the queen mother, “Humble yourselves. Sit down, for your rule, the crown of your comeliness, has come down.”
13.19: The cities of the South shall be shut up, with no one to open them. Yahuḏah shall be taken into exile, all of it. She shall be taken into exile, completely.
13.20: Lift up your eyes and see those who come from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, your lovely sheep?
13.21: What would you say when He visits you? For you have taught them to be chiefs, to be head over you. Do not pangs seize you, like a woman in labor?
13.22: And when you say in your heart, “Why has this come upon me?” It is because of your great wickedness that your skirts have been uncovered, your heels made bare.
13.23: Does a Kushite change his skin and a leopard its spots? You who are taught to do evil are also unable to do good!
13.24: “So I shall scatter them like stubble that passes away by the wind of the wilderness.
13.25: “This is your lot, your measured portion from Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “because you have forgotten Me, and trust in falsehood.
13.26: “I shall even draw your skirts over your face, and your shame shall be seen,
13.27: your adulteries and your neighings, the wickedness of your whoring! I have seen your abominations on the hills in the fields. Woe to you, O Yerushalayim! How long before you would be made clean?”

14.1: The word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that came to Yirmeyahu concerning the matter of droughts.
14.2: “Yahuḏah has mourned, and her gates have languished. They have mourned on the ground, and the cry of Yerushalayim has gone up.
14.3: “And their nobles have sent their little ones for water, they went to the cisterns and found no water, they returned with their vessels empty. They were put to shame, and blushed and covered their heads.
14.4: “Because the ground became cracked, for there has been no rain in the land. The ploughmen were put to shame, they covered their heads.
14.5: “Even the deer gave birth in the field, but left because there was no grass.
14.6: “And wild donkeys stood in the bare heights, they sniffed at the wind like jackals. Their eyes have failed because there was no grass.”
14.7: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, though our wickednesses witness against us, act, for Your Name’s sake. For our backslidings have been many, we have sinned against You.
14.8: O Expectation of Yisra’ĕl, its Savior in time of distress, why should You be like a stranger in the land, or like a traveler who turns aside to lodge?
14.9: Why should You be as one who is stunned, as a mighty man that is unable to save? Yet You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are in our midst, and Your Name has been called on us. Do not leave us!
14.10: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to this people, “So they have loved to wander, they have not restrained their feet. Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not accepted them. Now He remembers their wickedness and punishes their sins.”
14.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Do not pray for this people for their good.
14.12: “When they fast, I do not hear their cry. And when they offer burnt offering and grain offering, I do not accept them. Instead, I am consuming them by sword, and by scarcity of food, and by pestilence.”
14.13: But I said, “Ah, Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! See, the neḇi’im say to them, ‘You are not to see a sword, nor have scarcity of food, for I give you true peace in this place.’ ”
14.14: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “The neḇi’im naḇa falsehood in My Name. I have not sent them, nor commanded them, nor spoken to them. They naḇa to you a false vision, worthless divination, and the deceit of their own heart.
14.15: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning the neḇi’im who naḇa in My Name, whom I did not send, and who say, ‘Sword and scarcity of food shall not be in this land.’ ‘By sword and scarcity of food those neḇi’im shall be consumed!
14.16: ‘And the people to whom they naḇa shall be thrown out in the streets of Yerushalayim because of the scarcity of food and the sword, with no one to bury them - them nor their wives, their sons nor their daughters. For I shall pour their evil on them.’
14.17: “And you shall say this word to them, ‘Let my eyes flow with tears night and day, and let them not cease; for the maiden daughter of my people has been crushed with a mighty blow, with a very severe wound.
14.18: ‘If I go out to the field, then see those slain with the sword! And if I enter the city, then see those sick from scarcity of food! For both naḇi and kohĕn go about in a land they do not know.’ ”
14.19: Have You completely rejected Yahuḏah? Has Your being loathed Tsiyon? Why have You smitten us so that there is no healing for us? We looked for peace, but there was no good; and for the time of healing, but see - fear!
14.20: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, we know our wickedness and the wickedness of our fathers, for we have sinned against You.
14.21: Do not scorn us, for Your Name’s sake. Do not despise the throne of Your esteem. Remember, do not break Your Covenant with us.
14.22: Are there among the worthless idols of the nations any causing rain? And do the shamayim give showers? Are You not He, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim? And we wait for You, for You are the One who does all this.

15.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Even Mosheh and Shemu’ĕl were to stand before Me, My being is not toward this people. Send them away from My presence, let them go.
15.2: “And it shall be, when they say to you, ‘Where do we go?’ then you shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Those for death, to death. And those for the sword, to the sword. And those for scarcity of food, to scarcity of food. And those for captivity, to captivity.” ’
15.3: “And I shall appoint over them four kinds,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “the sword to slay, the dogs to drag, the birds of the shamayim and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
15.4: “And I shall make them for a horror to all the reigns of the earth, on account of Menashsheh son of Ḥizqiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, because of what he did in Yerushalayim.
15.5: “For who has compassion on you, O Yerushalayim? And who mourns for you? And who turns aside to ask how you are doing?
15.6: “You who have forsaken Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “you have gone backward. Therefore I shall stretch out My hand against you and destroy you. I have been weary of relenting!
15.7: “And I shall winnow them with a winnowing fan in the gates of the land. I shall bereave, I shall destroy My people. They would not turn back from their ways.
15.8: “Their widows shall be more numerous than the sand of the seas. I shall bring against them, against the mother of the young men, a ravager at noon. I shall cause terror and sudden alarm to fall on her, suddenly.
15.9: “She who has borne seven shall pine away. She shall breathe her last. Her sun shall go down while it is yet day. She shall be put to shame and be humiliated. And their remnant I give up to the sword before their enemies,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.10: Woe to me, my mother, that you have borne me, a man of strife and a man of contention to all the earth! I have neither lent for interest, nor have men lent to me for interest. All of them are reviling me.
15.11: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, “Did I not direct you for good? Did I not intercede for you in a time of evil and in a time of distress against the enemy?
15.12: “Does one break iron, iron or bronze from the north?
15.13: “Your wealth and your treasures I give as plunder, not for price, because of all your sins, even in all your borders.
15.14: “And I shall cause them to pass over with your enemies into a land which you did not know, for a fire is kindled in My displeasure, which burns upon you.”
15.15: You Yourself know, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Remember me and visit me, and take vengeance for me on these who persecute me. In Your patience, do not take me away. Know that for You I have suffered reproach.
15.16: Your Words were found, and I fed on them, and Your Word was to me the joy and rejoicing of my heart. For Your Name is called on me, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of hosts.
15.17: I have not sat in the company of the mockers, nor do I exult. I have sat alone because of Your hand, for You have filled me with displeasure.
15.18: Why is my pain without end and my wound incurable, which refuses to be healed? Are You to me like a failing stream, as waters not steadfast?
15.19: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “If you turn back, then I shall bring you back. Before Me you shall stand. And if you take out the precious from the worthless, you shall become as My mouth. Let them return to you, but do not return to them.
15.20: “And I shall make you to this people a strong bronze wall. And they shall fight against you, but not overcome you. For I am with you to save you and deliver you,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.21: “And I shall deliver you from the hand of evil-doers, and I shall ransom you from the grip of the ruthless.”

16.1: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
16.2: “Do not take a wife, nor have sons or daughters in this place.”
16.3: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning the sons and daughters who are born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bear them and their fathers who bring them forth in this land,
16.4: “They shall die of deaths from diseases, they shall not be lamented nor be buried, but be like dung on the face of the earth, and be consumed by sword and by scarcity of food. And their corpses shall be meat for the birds of the shamayim and for the beasts of the earth.”
16.5: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Do not enter the house of mourning, neither go to lament or mourn for them, for I have withdrawn My peace from this people,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “even the kindness and the compassions.
16.6: “Both great and small shall die in this land. They shall not be buried, and no one shall lament for them, or cut themselves, or make themselves bald for them.
16.7: “Neither shall they break bread in mourning for them to comfort them for the dead, nor give them the cup of comfort to drink for their father or their mother.
16.8: “Do not enter the house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and drink.”
16.9: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “See, before your eyes and in your days, I am making the voice of rejoicing and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride to cease in this place.
16.10: “And it shall be, when you declare to this people all these words, and they shall say to you, ‘Why has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 pronounced all this great evil against us? And what is our wickedness, and what is our sin that we have committed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim?’
16.11: then you shall say to them, ‘Because your fathers have forsaken Me,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and have walked after other mighty ones and served them and bowed themselves to them, and have forsaken Me, and did not guard My Torah.
16.12: ‘And you have done more evil than your fathers, for look, each one walks according to the stubbornness of his own evil heart, without listening to Me.
16.13: ‘So I shall throw you out of this land into a land that you do not know, neither you nor your fathers. And there you shall serve other mighty ones day and night, where I show you no favor.’
16.14: “Therefore see, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when it is no longer said, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives who brought up the children of Yisra’ĕl from the land of Mitsrayim,’
16.15: but, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives who brought up the children of Yisra’ĕl from the land of the north and from all the lands where He had driven them.’ For I shall bring them back into their land I gave to their fathers.
16.16: “See, I am sending for many fishermen,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and they shall fish them. And after that I shall send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain and every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks.
16.17: “For My eyes are on all their ways; they have not been hidden from My face, nor has their wickedness been hidden from My eyes.
16.18: “And first I shall repay double for their wickedness and their sin, because they have defiled My land with the dead bodies of their filthiness, and have filled My inheritance with their abominations.”
16.19: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, my strength and my stronghold and my refuge, in the day of distress the gentiles shall come to You from the ends of the earth and say, “Our fathers have inherited only falsehood, futility, and there is no value in them.”
16.20: Would a man make mighty ones for himself, which are not mighty ones?
16.21: “Therefore see, I am causing them to know, this time I cause them to know My hand and My might. And they shall know that My Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!”

17.1: “The sin of Yahuḏah is written with a pen of iron, engraved with the point of a diamond on the tablet of their heart, and on the horns of your altars,
17.2: while their children remember their altars and their Ashĕrim by the spreading trees on the high hills.
17.3: “My mountain in the field, I give as plunder, your wealth, all your treasures, your high places of sin, throughout all your borders.
17.4: “And you, even of yourself, shall let go of your inheritance which I gave you. And I shall make you serve your enemies in a land which you have not known, for you have kindled a fire in My displeasure which burns forever.”
17.5: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart turns away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.6: “For he shall be like a shrub in the desert, and not see when good comes, and shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, a salt land that is not inhabited.
17.7: “Baruḵ is the man who trusts in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and whose trust is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.8: “For he shall be like a tree planted by the waters, which spreads out its roots by the river, and does not see when heat comes. And his leaf shall be green, and in the year of drought he is not anxious, nor does he cease from yielding fruit.
17.9: “The heart is crooked above all, and desperately sick - who shall know it?
17.10: “I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, search the heart, I try the kidneys, and give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds.
17.11: “As a partridge that broods but does not hatch, so is he who gets riches, but not by right. It leaves him in the midst of his days, and at his end he is a fool.”
17.12: An esteemed throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our Miqdash.
17.13: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the expectation of Yisra’ĕl, all who forsake You are put to shame. “Those who depart from Me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Fountain of living waters.”
17.14: Heal me, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, so that I am healed. Save me, so that I am saved, for You are my praise.
17.15: See, they say to me, “Where is the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? Let it come now!”
17.16: And I have not run away from being a shepherd who follows You, nor have I longed for the woeful day. You Yourself have known, that which came out of my lips was before You.
17.17: Do not be a ruin to me, You are my shelter in the day of evil.
17.18: Let these who persecute me be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be broken, but do not let me be broken. Bring on them the day of evil, and destroy them with double destruction!
17.19: Thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Go and stand in the gate of the children of the people, by which the melaḵim of Yahuḏah come in and by which they go out, and in all the gates of Yerushalayim.
17.20: “And you shall say to them, ‘Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, you melaḵim of Yahuḏah, and all Yahuḏah, and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, who enter by these gates.
17.21: ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Guard yourselves, and bear no burden on the Shabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Yerushalayim,
17.22: nor take a burden out of your houses on the Shabbath day, nor do any work. And you shall qadosh the Shabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.
17.23: “But they did not obey, or incline their ear, and they made their neck stiff not to hear and not to receive instruction.
17.24: “And it shall be, if you diligently obey Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the Shabbath day, and qadosh the Shabbath day, to do no work in it,
17.25: then melaḵim and heads sitting on the throne of Dawiḏ shall enter in through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their heads - the men of Yahuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim. And this city shall be inhabited forever.
17.26: “And they shall come from the cities of Yahuḏah and from the places around Yerushalayim, and from the land of Binyamin and from the low country, from the mountains and from the Negeḇ, bringing burnt offerings and slaughterings, grain offerings and incense, bringing offerings of praise to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.27: “But if you do not obey Me to qadosh the Shabbath day, and not to bear a burden when entering the gates of Yerushalayim on the Shabbath day, then I shall kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall consume the palaces of Yerushalayim, and not be quenched.” ’ ”

18.1: The word which came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
18.2: “Arise, and go down to the potter’s house, and there I let you hear My words.”
18.3: So I went down to the potter’s house, and saw him doing a piece of work on the wheel.
18.4: And the vessel that he made of clay was ruined in the hand of the potter, so he remade it into another vessel, as it seemed good to the potter to do.
18.5: Then the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
18.6: “O house of Yisra’ĕl, am I not able to do with you as this potter?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “Look, as the clay is in the hand of the potter, so are you in My hand, O house of Yisra’ĕl!
18.7: “The moment I speak concerning a nation and concerning a reign, to pluck up, to pull down, and to destroy it,
18.8: and that nation shall turn from its evil because I have spoken against it, then I shall repent of the evil that I thought to do to it.
18.9: “And the moment I speak concerning a nation and concerning a reign, to build and to plant it,
18.10: and it shall do evil in My eyes in not obeying My voice, then I shall repent concerning the good with which I spoke of doing to it.
18.11: “And now, speak to the men of Yahuḏah and to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am forming evil and devising a plan against you. Return now every one from his evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.” ’ ”
18.12: But they shall say, “It is no use! For we walk according to our own plans, and we do each one the stubbornness of his evil heart.”
18.13: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Ask now among the nations, who has heard the like of this? The maiden of Yisra’ĕl has done what is most horrible.
18.14: “Does the snow of Leḇanon cease from the rock of the field? Or the cool flowing waters from afar dry up?
18.15: “But My people have forgotten Me, they have burned incense to what is false, and they have stumbled from their ways, from the ancient paths, to walk in bypaths and not on a highway,
18.16: to make their land become a ruin, a hissing forever - everyone who passes by it is appalled and shakes his head.
18.17: “I shall scatter them as with an east wind before the enemy; I shall show them the back and not the face in the day of their calamity.”
18.18: Then they said, “Come and let us devise plans against Yirmeyahu, for the Torah shall not perish from the kohĕn, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the naḇi. Come and let us smite him with the tongue, and let us not listen to any of his words.”
18.19: Attend to me, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and listen to the voice of my adversaries!
18.20: Should good be repaid with evil? For they have dug a pit for my life. Remember that I stood before You to speak good for them, and to turn away Your wrath from them.
18.21: So give their children over to scarcity of food, and hand them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives become widows and bereaved of their children. Let their men be put to death, their young men be smitten by the sword in battle.
18.22: Let a cry be heard from their houses, when You bring a raiding party suddenly upon them. For they have dug a pit to take me, and laid snares for my feet.
18.23: But You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You know all their counsel against me, to slay me. Do not pardon their wickedness, nor blot out their sin from Your presence, and let them be overthrown before You. Deal with them in the time of Your displeasure.

19.1: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Go and get a potter’s earthen jug, and take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the kohenim.
19.2: “Then you shall go out to the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, which is by the entry of the Potsherd Gate, and shall proclaim there the words that I speak to you,
19.3: and shall say, ‘Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, melaḵim of Yahuḏah and inhabitants of Yerushalayim. Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “See, I am bringing evil on this place, that makes the ears tingle of all who hear it.
19.4: “Because they have forsaken Me and have profaned this place, and have burned incense in it to other mighty ones whom neither they, their fathers, nor the melaḵim of Yahuḏah have known, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocents,
19.5: and have built the high places of Ba’al, to burn their sons with fire for burnt offerings to Ba’al, which I did not command or speak, nor did it come into My heart.
19.6: “Therefore see, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that this place shall no more be called Topheth or the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.
19.7: “And I shall pour out the counsel of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim in this place, and I shall make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hands of those who seek their lives. And I shall give their corpses as meat for the birds of the shamayim and for the beasts of the earth.
19.8: “And I shall make this city a ruin, and a hissing - everyone who passes by it is appalled and hisses because of all its plagues.
19.9: “And I shall make them to eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and eat one another’s flesh in the siege and in the distress with which their enemies and those who seek their lives distress them.” ’
19.10: “And you shall break the jug before the eyes of the men who go with you,
19.11: and shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “Even so I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter’s vessel, which one is unable to repair again. And let them bury them in Topheth till there is no place to bury.
19.12: “This is what I shall do to this place,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and to its inhabitants, so as to make this city like Topheth.
19.13: “And the houses of Yerushalayim and the houses of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah shall be as unclean as the place of Topheth, because of all the houses on whose roofs they have burned incense to all the host of the shamayim, and poured out drink offerings to other mighty ones.” ’ ”
19.14: And when Yirmeyahu returned from Topheth, where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had sent him to naḇa, he stood in the courtyard of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and said to all the people,
19.15: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘See, I am bringing on this city and on all her towns all the evil that I have pronounced against it, because they have stiffened their necks so as not to hear My Words.’ ”

2.1: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
2.2: “Go, and you shall cry in the hearing of Yerushalayim, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I remember you, the kindness of your youth, the love of your bridehood, when you went after Me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.
2.3: “Yisra’ĕl was qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the first-fruits of His increase. All who ate of it became guilty - evil came upon them,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”
2.4: Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O house of Ya’aqoḇ and all the clans of the house of Yisra’ĕl.
2.5: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “What unrighteousness have your fathers found in Me, that they have gone far from Me, and went after worthlessness, became worthless?
2.6: “And did not they say, ‘Where is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who brought us up out of the land of Mitsrayim, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and pits, through a land of drought and the shadow of death, a land that no one passed through and where no one dwelt?’
2.7: “Then I brought you into a garden land, to eat its fruit and its goodness. But when you entered, you defiled My land and made My inheritance an abomination.
2.8: “The kohenim did not say, ‘Where is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?’ And those who handle the Torah did not know Me, and the shepherds transgressed against Me, and the neḇi’im naḇu by Ba’al, and walked after no value.
2.9: “Therefore I still contend with you,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and with your children’s children I contend.
2.10: “For, pass beyond the isles of Kittim and see, and send to Qĕḏar and observe well, and see if there has been any like this.
2.11: “Has a nation changed its mighty ones, which are not mighty ones? But My people have changed My esteem for that which does not profit.
2.12: “Be amazed, O shamayim, at this, and be frightened, be utterly dried up,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.13: “For My people have done two evils: they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, to hew out for themselves cisterns, cracked cisterns, which do not hold water.
2.14: “Is Yisra’ĕl a servant? Was he born in the house? Why is he given to plunder?
2.15: “The young lions roared at him, they growled, and made his land waste; his cities have been burned, without inhabitant.
2.16: “Even the sons of Noph and of Taḥpanḥes have shaven the crown of your head.
2.17: “Have you not done this to yourself, by forsaking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim when He led you in the way?
2.18: “And now why take the way to Mitsrayim, to drink the waters of Shiḥor? Or why take the way to Ashshur, to drink the waters of the River?
2.19: “Your own evil instructs you, and your backslidings reprove you. Know therefore and see that it is evil and bitter that you have forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and that My reverence is not in you,” declares Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts.
2.20: “For of old you have broken your yoke and tore off your bonds. And you said, ‘I am not serving!’ When on every high hill and under every green tree you lay down, a whore.
2.21: “Yet I had planted you a choice vine, all of it a true seed. How then have you turned before Me into the degenerate plant of a strange vine?
2.22: “Although you wash yourself with lye, and use much soap, yet your wickedness is ingrained before Me,” declares Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.23: “How do you say, ‘I am not defiled, I have not gone after the Ba’als’? See your way in the valley, know what you have done: a swift dromedary breaking loose in her ways,
2.24: a wild donkey used to the wilderness, sniffing the wind in the desire of her being - in her time of mating, who turns her away? All those who seek her need not weary themselves; in her month they find her.
2.25: “Keep your foot from being bare, and your throat from thirst. But you said, ‘It is useless, because I love strangers, and after them I go.’
2.26: “As the thief is ashamed when he is found out, so is the house of Yisra’ĕl ashamed - they and their melaḵim and their heads, and their kohenim and their neḇi’im,
2.27: saying to a tree, ‘You are my father,’ and to a stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’ For they have turned their back to Me, and not their face. But in the time of their calamity they say, ‘Arise and save us.’
2.28: “But where are your mighty ones that you have made for yourselves? Let them arise if they save you in the time of your calamity. Because your mighty ones have become as many as your cities, O Yahuḏah.
2.29: “Why do you complain to Me? You all have transgressed against Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.30: “In vain have I smitten your children - they received no instruction. Your sword has devoured your neḇi’im like a destroying lion.
2.31: “O generation, see the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! Have I been a wilderness to Yisra’ĕl, or a land of darkness? Why do My people say, ‘We have broken loose; we come to You no more’?
2.32: “Would a maiden forget her ornaments, or a bride her headband? Yet My people have forgotten Me, days without number.
2.33: “Why do you embellish your way to seek love? Therefore you have even taught the evil women your ways.
2.34: “Even on your skirts is found the blood of the lives of the poor innocents. You did not find them breaking in, but in spite of all these,
2.35: you say, ‘Because I am innocent, certainly His displeasure shall turn from me.’ See, I shall bring judgment on you, because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’
2.36: “Why do you go about so much to change your way? Even of Mitsrayim you are to be ashamed, as you were ashamed of Ashshur.
2.37: “Even from this one you shall go forth, with your hands on your head. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has rejected those you trust, and you shall not prosper by them,

20.1: And Pashḥur son of Immĕr, the kohĕn who was also chief governor in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, heard that Yirmeyahu naḇu these words.
20.2: And Pashḥur struck Yirmeyahu the naḇi, and put him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Binyamin, which was by the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.3: And it came to be on the next day that Pashḥur brought Yirmeyahu out of the stocks, and Yirmeyahu said to him, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not called your name Pashḥur, but Maḡor-Missaḇiḇ.
20.4: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I am making you a fear to yourself and to all your loved ones. And they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, while your eyes see it. And I shall give all Yahuḏah into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and he shall exile them to Baḇel and smite them with the sword.
20.5: ‘And I shall give all the wealth of this city and all its labor, and all its valuables, and all the treasures of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah, I give into the hand of their enemies, who shall plunder them, seize them, and shall bring them to Baḇel.
20.6: ‘And you, Pashḥur, and all who dwell in your house, shall go into captivity, and enter into Baḇel. And there you shall die, and be buried there, you and all your friends, to whom you have naḇu falsehood.’ ”
20.7: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You deluded me, and I was deluded. You are stronger than I, and have prevailed. I have been ridiculed all day long, everyone mocks me.
20.8: For when I speak, I cry out, proclaiming violence and ruin. Because the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was made to me a reproach and a mockery daily.
20.9: Whenever I said, “Let me not mention Him, nor speak in His Name again,” it was in my heart like a burning fire shut up in my bones. And I became weary of holding it back, and was helpless.
20.10: For I heard many mocking, “Fear on every side!” “Expose,” they say, “let us expose him!” All my friends watched for my stumbling, “He might be lured away, so that we prevail against him, and take our revenge on him.”
20.11: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with me like a mighty, awesome One. Therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and not prevail. They shall be greatly ashamed, for they have not acted wisely - an everlasting reproach never to be forgotten.
20.12: But, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, trying the righteous, and seeing the kidneys and heart, let me see Your vengeance on them, for I have revealed my cause to You.
20.13: Sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! Hallelu-𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! For He has delivered the being of the poor from the hand of evil ones.
20.14: Cursed be the day in which I was born! Let the day not be baruḵ in which my mother bore me!
20.15: Let the man be cursed who brought news to my father, saying, “A male child has been born to you,” making him very glad.
20.16: And let that man be like the cities which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 overthrew, and repented not. Let him hear the cry in the morning and the shouting at noon,
20.17: because I was not slain from the womb, so that my mother should have been my grave and her womb forever great.
20.18: Why did I come forth from the womb to see toil and sorrow, and spend my days in shame?

21.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 when Meleḵ Tsiḏqiyahu sent to him Pashḥur son of Malkiyah, and Tsephanyah the son of Ma’asĕyah, the kohĕn, saying,
21.2: “Please inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on our behalf, for Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel is fighting against us. It might be that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 deals with us according to all His wondrous works, so that he withdraws from us.”
21.3: But Yirmeyahu said to them, “Say this to Tsiḏqiyahu,
21.4: ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “See, I am turning back the weapons of battle that are in your hands, with which you fight against the meleḵ of Baḇel and the Kasdites who besiege you outside the wall. And I shall gather them inside this city.
21.5: “And I Myself shall fight against you with an outstretched hand, and with a strong arm, even in displeasure and rage and great wrath.
21.6: “And I shall smite the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast - let them die of a great pestilence.
21.7: “And afterward,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I give Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, his servants and the people, and such as are left in this city from the pestilence and the sword and the scarcity of food, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those who seek their life. And he shall smite them with the edge of the sword. He shall not pardon them, nor spare nor have compassion.” ’
21.8: “You shall also say to this people, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I lay before you the way of life and the way of death.
21.9: “Whoever stays in this city dies by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence. But whoever goes out and shall go over to the Kasdites who besiege you, is going to live, and his life shall be as a prize to him.
21.10: “For I have turned My face against this city for evil and not for good,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “It is given into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and he shall burn it with fire.” ’
21.11: “And to the house of the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, ‘Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
21.12: ‘O house of Dawiḏ! Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Render right-ruling in the morning, and deliver him who has been robbed out of the hand of the oppressor, lest My wrath go out like fire and burn, with no one to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.
21.13: “See, I am against you, O inhabitant of the valley, rock of the plain,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “who are saying, ‘Who would come down against us? And who would come into our dwellings?’
21.14: “And I shall punish you according to the fruit of your deeds,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄., “And I shall kindle a fire in its forest, and it shall consume all that is around her.” ’ ”

22.1: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Go down to the house of the meleḵ of Yahuḏah. And there you shall speak this word,
22.2: and shall say, ‘Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O meleḵ of Yahuḏah, you who sit on the throne of Dawiḏ, you and your servants and your people who enter these gates!
22.3: ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Do right-ruling and righteousness, and deliver him who is robbed out of the hand of the oppressor. Do not maltreat nor do violence to the stranger, the fatherless, or the widow, nor shed innocent blood in this place.
22.4: “For if you certainly do this word, then there shall enter in by the gates of this house melaḵim sitting on the throne of Dawiḏ, riding on horses and in chariots, he and his servants and his people.
22.5: “But if you do not obey these words, I swear by Myself,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that this house shall become a ruin.” ’ ”
22.6: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to the house of the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, “You are as Gil’aḏ to Me, the head of Leḇanon. But I shall make you a wilderness, and cities which are not inhabited.
22.7: “And I shall prepare destroyers against you, each with his weapons. And they shall cut down your choice cedars and throw them into the fire.
22.8: “And many gentiles shall pass by this city, and they shall say to one another, ‘Why has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 done so to this great city?’
22.9: “Then they shall say, ‘Because they have forsaken the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, and bowed themselves to other mighty ones and served them.’ ”
22.10: Do not weep for the dead, nor mourn for him. Weep bitterly for him who goes away, for he shall never come back nor see the land of his birth.
22.11: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning Shallum son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, who reigned instead of Yoshiyahu his father, who went from this place, “He shall never come back,
22.12: but he shall die in the place where they have exiled him, and not see this land again.
22.13: “Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness and his rooms without Right-Ruling, who uses his neighbor’s service without wages and does not give him his wages,
22.14: who says, ‘I am going to build myself a wide house with spacious rooms, and cut out windows for it, paneling it with cedar and painting it in red.’
22.15: “Do you reign because you enclose yourself in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink, and do right-ruling and righteousness? Then it was well with him.
22.16: “He defended the cause of the poor and needy - then it was well. Was this not to know Me?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.17: “But your eyes and your heart are only upon your own greedy gain, and on shedding innocent blood, and on oppression and on doing violence.”
22.18: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning Yahoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, “Let them not lament for him: ‘Alas, my brother!’ or ‘Alas, my sister!’ Let them not lament for him: ‘Alas, master!’ or ‘Alas, his excellency!’
22.19: “He shall be buried with the burial of a donkey, dragged and thrown outside the gates of Yerushalayim.
22.20: “Go up to Leḇanon, and cry out, and lift up your voice in Bashan. And cry from Aḇarim, for all your lovers are destroyed.
22.21: “I have spoken to you in your ease, but you said, ‘I do not listen.’ This has been your way from your youth, for you did not obey My voice.
22.22: “Let all your shepherds be devoured by the wind, and your lovers go into captivity. Then you shall be ashamed and humiliated for all your evil.
22.23: “You who dwell in Leḇanon, being nested in the cedars, how you shall groan when pangs come upon you, like the pains of a woman giving birth!
22.24: “As I live,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “though Konyahu son of Yahoyaqim, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, were the signet on My right hand, I would still pull you off from there;
22.25: and I shall give you into the hand of those who seek your life, and into the hand of those whose face you fear, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel and the hand of the Kasdites.
22.26: “And I shall hurl you out, and your mother who bore you, into another land where you were not born, and there you shall die.
22.27: “But they shall not return to the land to which their being yearns to return.
22.28: “Is this man Konyahu a despised broken pot, or an undesirable vessel? Why are they hurled out, he and his descendants, and cast into a land which they do not know?
22.29: “O land, land, land! Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
22.30: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Write this man down as childless, a strong man who is not to prosper in his days, for none of his descendants shall prosper, sitting on the throne of Dawiḏ, or rule any more in Yahuḏah.’ ”

23.1: “Woe to the shepherds destroying and scattering the sheep of My pasture!” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.2: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl against the shepherds who feed My people, “You have scattered My flock, driven them away, and have not tended them. See, I am punishing you for the evil of your deeds,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.3: “Therefore I shall gather the remnant of My flock out of all the lands where I have driven them, and shall bring them back to their fold. And they shall bear and increase.
23.4: “And I shall raise up shepherds over them, and they shall feed them. And they shall fear no more, nor be discouraged, nor shall they be lacking,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.5: “See, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when I shall raise for Dawiḏ a Branch of righteousness, and a Meleḵ shall reign and act wisely, and shall do right-ruling and righteousness in the earth.
23.6: “In His days Yahuḏah shall be saved, and Yisra’ĕl dwell safely. And this is His Name whereby He shall be called: ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Tsidqĕnu.’
23.7: “Therefore, see, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when they shall say no more, ‘As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives who brought up the children of Yisra’ĕl out of the land of Mitsrayim,’
23.8: but, ‘As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives who brought up and led the seed of the house of Yisra’ĕl out of the land of the north and from all the lands where I had driven them.’ And they shall dwell on their own land.”
23.9: My heart within me is broken because of the neḇi’im; all my bones shake. I am like a drunken man, and like a man overcome by wine, because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and because of His qodesh words.
23.10: For the land is filled with adulterers; for the land mourns because of a curse. The pastures of the wilderness are dried up. And their course is evil, and their might is not right.
23.11: “For both naḇi and kohĕn have become defiled. Even in My house I have found their evil,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.12: “Therefore their way is to them like slippery ways in the dark. They are driven on and they shall fall in them. For I bring evil on them, the year of their punishment,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.13: “And I have seen folly in the neḇi’im of Shomeron: they naḇu by Ba’al and led My people Yisra’ĕl astray.
23.14: “And among the neḇi’im of Yerushalayim I have seen a horrible matter: committing adultery and walking in falsehood. And they strengthen the hands of evil ones, so that no one turns back from his evil. All of them are like Seḏom to Me, and her inhabitants like Amorah.
23.15: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts concerning the neḇi’im, ‘See, I am making them eat wormwood, and shall make them drink poisoned water. For defilement has gone out into all the land from the neḇi’im of Yerushalayim.’ ”
23.16: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “Do not listen to the words of the neḇi’im who naḇa to you, they lead you astray. They speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.17: “They keep on saying to those who despise Me, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said you shall have peace.’ And to all who walk according to the stubbornness of their own heart, ‘No evil comes upon you.’ ”
23.18: For who has stood in the counsel of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and has seen and heard His word? Who has listened to His word and obeyed it?
23.19: See, a storm of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall go forth in a rage, a whirling storm! It whirls on the head of the wicked.
23.20: The displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall not turn back until He has done and established the purposes of His heart. In the latter days you shall understand it perfectly.
23.21: “I did not send these neḇi’im, yet they ran. I have not spoken to them, yet they naḇu.
23.22: “But if they had stood in My counsel, then they would have let My people hear My Words, and they would have turned them from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.
23.23: “Am I an Elohim close by,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and not an Elohim afar off?
23.24: “If anyone is hidden in secret places, would I not see him?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “Do I not fill the shamayim and earth?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.25: “I have heard what the neḇi’im have said who naḇa falsehood in My Name, saying, ‘I have dreamed, I have dreamed!’
23.26: “Till when shall it be in the heart of the neḇi’im? - the neḇi’im of falsehood and neḇi’im of the deceit of their own heart,
23.27: who try to make My people forget My Name by their dreams which everyone relates to his neighbor, as their fathers forgot My Name for Ba’al.
23.28: “The naḇi who has a dream, let him relate the dream, and he who has My Word, let him speak My Word in truth. What is the chaff to the wheat?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.29: “Is not My Word like a fire?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and like a hammer that shatters a rock?
23.30: “Therefore see, I am against the neḇi’im,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “who steal My Words every one from his neighbor.
23.31: “See, I am against the neḇi’im,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “who use their tongues and say, ‘He declares.’
23.32: “See, I am against those who naḇa false dreams,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and relate them, and lead My people astray by their falsehoods and by their reckless boasting. But I Myself did not send them nor have I commanded them. And they do not profit this people at all,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.33: “And when these people or the naḇi or the kohĕn ask you, saying, ‘What is the message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?’ then you shall say to them, ‘What message?’ I shall forsake you,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.34: “As for the naḇi and the kohĕn and the people who say, ‘The message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,’ I shall punish that man and his house.
23.35: “This is what each one says to his neighbor, and each one to his brother, ‘What has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answered?’ and, ‘What has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoken?’
23.36: “But the message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 you no longer remember! For every man’s message is his own word, for you have changed the Words of the living Elohim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, our Elohim!
23.37: “This is what you say to the naḇi, ‘What has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answered you?’ and, ‘What has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoken?’
23.38: “But since you say, ‘The message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!’ therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Because you say this word, “The message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!” and I have sent to you, saying, “Do not say, ‘The message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!’ ”
23.39: therefore see, I, I shall utterly forget you and cast you away from My presence, along with the city that I gave you and your fathers.
23.40: ‘And I shall put an everlasting reproach on you, and an everlasting shame that is not forgotten.’ ”

24.1: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showed me, and look, there were two baskets of figs put before the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, after Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel had exiled Yeḵonyahu son of Yahoyaqim, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and the heads of Yahuḏah with the craftsmen and smiths, from Yerushalayim, and had brought them to Baḇel.
24.2: One basket had very good figs, like the figs that are first ripe. And the other basket had very spoilt figs which could not be eaten, they were so spoilt.”
24.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “What do you see, Yirmeyahu?” And I said, “Figs, the good figs, very good. And the spoilt, very spoilt, which could not be eaten, they are so spoilt.”
24.4: Again the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
24.5: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Like these good figs, so do I acknowledge the exiles of Yahuḏah, whom I have sent out of this place for their own good, into the land of the Kasdites.
24.6: ‘And I shall lay My eyes on them for good, and shall bring them back to this land. And I shall build them and not pull them down, and shall plant them and not pluck them up.
24.7: ‘And I shall give them a heart to know Me, that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they shall be My people and I shall be their Elohim, for they shall turn back to Me with all their heart.
24.8: ‘And as the spoilt figs that could not be eaten because they are so spoilt,’ for thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘so do I give up Tsiḏqiyahu, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, his heads, the rest of Yerushalayim who remain in this land, and those who dwell in the land of Mitsrayim.
24.9: ‘And I shall make them a horror to all the reigns of the earth, for evil, to be a reproach and a byword, a mockery and a curse, in all the places to which I drive them.
24.10: ‘And I shall send the sword, the scarcity of food, and the pestilence among them, till they are consumed from the land that I gave to them and their fathers.’ ”

25.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu concerning all the people of Yahuḏah, in the fourth year of Yahoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, which was the first year of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel,
25.2: which Yirmeyahu the naḇi spoke to all the people of Yahuḏah and to all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, saying,
25.3: “From the thirteenth year of Yoshiyahu son of Amon, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, even to this day, this is the twenty-third year in which the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has come to me. And I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, but you have not listened.
25.4: “Moreover, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent to you all His servants the neḇi’im, rising early and sending them, but you have not listened nor inclined your ear to hear,
25.5: saying, ‘Turn back now everyone from his evil way and from the evil of your deeds, and dwell on the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given to you and your fathers forever and ever.
25.6: ‘And do not go after other mighty ones to serve them and to bow down to them. And do not provoke Me with the works of your hands, so that I do you no evil.’
25.7: “But you did not listen to Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “so as to provoke Me with the works of your hands, for your own evil.
25.8: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, ‘Because you did not obey My Words,
25.9: see, I am sending and taking all the tribes of the north,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel, My servant, and shall bring them against this land and against its inhabitants, and against these nations all around, and shall put them under the ban, and make them an astonishment, and a hissing, and everlasting ruins.
25.10: ‘And I shall banish from them the voice of rejoicing and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
25.11: ‘And all this land shall be a ruin and a waste, and these nations shall serve the meleḵ of Baḇel seventy years.
25.12: ‘And it shall be, when seventy years are completed, that I shall punish the meleḵ of Baḇel and that nation, the land of the Kasdites, for their wickedness,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and shall make it everlasting ruins.
25.13: ‘And I shall bring on that land all My words which I have pronounced against it, all that is written in this book, which Yirmeyahu has naḇu concerning all the nations.
25.14: ‘For they too shall be enslaved by many nations and great melaḵim. And I shall repay them according to their deeds and according to the works of their hands.’ ”
25.15: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl to me, “Take this wine cup of wrath from My hand, and make all the nations, to whom I send you, drink it.
25.16: “And they shall drink, and shake, and go mad because of the sword that I am sending among them.”
25.17: I then took the cup from the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and made all the nations drink, to whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had sent me;
25.18: Yerushalayim and the cities of Yahuḏah, and its melaḵim, its heads, to make them a ruin, an object of astonishment, a hissing, and a curse, as it is this day;
25.19: Pharaoh meleḵ of Mitsrayim, and his servants, and his heads, and all his people;
25.20: and all the mixed multitude, and all the melaḵim of the land of Uts, and all the melaḵim of the land of the Pelishtites - even Ashqelon, and Azzah, and Eqron, and the remnant of Ashdoḏ;
25.21: Eḏom, and Mo’aḇ, and the children of Ammon;
25.22: and all the melaḵim of Tsor, and all the melaḵim of Tsiḏon, and the melaḵim of the coastlands which are beyond the sea;
25.23: Deḏan, and Tĕma, and Buz, and all who are in the farthest corners;
25.24: and all the melaḵim of Araḇia and all the melaḵim of the mixed multitude who dwell in the wilderness;
25.25: and all the melaḵim of Zimri, and all the melaḵim of Ĕylam, and all the melaḵim of the Maḏites;
25.26: and all the melaḵim of the north, far and near, one with another, and all the reigns of the earth which are on the face of the ground. Also the meleḵ of Shĕshaḵ shall drink after them.
25.27: “And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Drink, be drunk, and vomit! Fall and rise no more, because of the sword which I am sending among you.” ’
25.28: “And it shall be, when they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, then you shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “You shall drink!
25.29: “For look, I am beginning to bring evil upon the city which is called by My Name, and should you be entirely unpunished? You are not going unpunished, for I am calling for a sword on all the inhabitants of the earth,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts.’
25.30: “And you shall naḇa against them all these words, and say to them, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 roars from on high, and utters His voice from His qodesh dwelling place. He roars mightily over His fold, a shout as those who tread the grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth.
25.31: “Tumult shall come to the ends of the earth, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has a controversy with the nations. He shall enter into judgment with all flesh. The wicked He shall give to the sword,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
25.32: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “See, evil is going forth from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind is raised up from the farthest parts of the earth.
25.33: “And in that day the slain of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be from one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth. They shall not be lamented, or gathered, or buried, for they are dung on the face of the ground.
25.34: “Howl, you shepherds, and cry! And roll yourselves in ashes, you leaders of the flock! For the days of your slaughter and your scatterings are completed, and you shall fall like a choice vessel.
25.35: “And a place of refuge shall perish from the shepherds, and escape from the leaders of the flock.
25.36: “Hear the cry of the shepherds, and a wailing of the leaders of the flock, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is ravaging their pasture!
25.37: “And the pastures of peace shall be cut down because of the burning displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
25.38: “Like a lion He shall leave His hiding place, for their land shall become a waste because of the sword of oppressors, and because of His burning displeasure.”

26.1: In the beginning of the reign of Yahoyaqim the son of Yoshiyahu, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, this word came from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
26.2: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Stand in the courtyard of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and speak to all the cities of Yahuḏah, which come to bow themselves in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all the words that I command you to speak to them. Do not diminish a word.
26.3: ‘If so be that they listen and each turn from his evil way, then I shall repent of the evil that I plan to do to them, because of the evil of their deeds.’
26.4: “And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “If you do not listen to Me, to walk in My Torah which I put before you,
26.5: to listen to the words of My servants the neḇi’im I am sending you, even rising up early and sending them - though you have not listened -
26.6: then I shall make this House like Shiloh, and make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.” ’ ”
26.7: And the kohenim and the neḇi’im and all the people heard Yirmeyahu speaking these words in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.8: And it came to be, when Yirmeyahu had ended speaking all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded him to speak to all the people, that the kohenim and the neḇi’im and all the people seized him, saying, “You shall certainly die!
26.9: “Why have you naḇu in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, ‘This House shall be like Shiloh, and this city be dried up, without an inhabitant’?” And all the people were gathered against Yirmeyahu in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.10: And the heads of Yahuḏah heard this, and they came up from the meleḵ’s house to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and sat down in the entrance of the new gate of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.11: And the kohenim and the neḇi’im spoke to the heads and all the people, saying, “A death sentence for this man! For he has naḇu against this city, as you have heard with your ears.”
26.12: And Yirmeyahu spoke to all the heads and all the people, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent me to naḇa against this house and against this city with all the words you heard.
26.13: “And now, make good your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall relent concerning the evil He has pronounced against you.
26.14: “And I, look I am in your hand. Do with me as seems good and right to you.
26.15: “But know for certain that if you put me to death, you are bringing innocent blood on yourselves, and on this city, and on its inhabitants. For truly 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing.”
26.16: Then the heads and all the people said to the kohenim and the neḇi’im, “No death sentence for this man. For he has spoken to us in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.”
26.17: And some of the elders of the land rose up and spoke to all the assembly of the people, saying,
26.18: “Miḵayah of Moresheth naḇu in the days of Ḥizqiyahu the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and he spoke to all the people of Yahuḏah, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “Tsiyon shall become a ploughed field, and Yerushalayim be heaps, and the mountain of the House like the bare hills of the forest.” ’
26.19: “Did Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah and all Yahuḏah indeed put him to death? Did he not revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and seek the favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 relented concerning the evil which He had pronounced against them. But we are doing great evil against ourselves.”
26.20: There was however a man who naḇu in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Uriyahu the son of Shemayahu of Qiryath Ye’arim, who naḇu against this city and against this land according to all the words of Yirmeyahu.
26.21: And when Yahoyaqim the meleḵ, with all his mighty men and all the heads, heard his words, the meleḵ sought to put him to death. But Uriyahu heard of it, and was afraid and fled, and went to Mitsrayim.
26.22: Then Yahoyaqim the meleḵ sent men to Mitsrayim: Elnathan the son of Aḵbor, and some men who went with him to Mitsrayim.
26.23: And they brought Uriyahu from Mitsrayim and brought him to Yahoyaqim the meleḵ, who smote him with the sword and threw his dead body into the graves of the common people.
26.24: However, the hand of Aḥiqam son of Shaphan was with Yirmeyahu, so as not to give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.

27.1: In the beginning of the reign of Yahoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, this word came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
27.2: “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Make for yourselves bands and yokes. Then you shall put them on your neck,
27.3: and shall send them to the meleḵ of Eḏom, and the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ, and the meleḵ of the Ammonites, and the meleḵ of Tsor, and the meleḵ of Tsiḏon, by the hand of the messengers who come to Yerushalayim to Tsiḏqiyahu, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah.
27.4: ‘And you shall command them to say to their masters, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Say this to your masters,’
27.5: ‘I have made the earth, the man and the beast that are on the face of the earth, by My great power and by My outstretched arm. And I shall give it to whom it seemed right in My eyes.
27.6: ‘And now, I have given all these lands into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel, My servant. And the beasts of the field I have also given him to serve him.
27.7: ‘And all nations shall serve him and his son and his son’s son, until the time of his land comes. And then many nations and great melaḵim shall make him serve them.
27.8: ‘And it shall be, the nation and reign that do not serve Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel, and the one that does not put its neck under the yoke of the meleḵ of Baḇel, that nation I shall punish,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘with the sword, and the scarcity of food, and the pestilence, until I have consumed them by his hand.
27.9: ‘So do not listen to your neḇi’im, or to your diviners, or to your dreamers, or to your observers of clouds, or your sorcerers, who speak to you, saying, “Do not serve the meleḵ of Baḇel.”
27.10: ‘For they naḇa falsehood to you, to remove you far from your land. And I shall drive you out, and you shall perish.
27.11: ‘But the nations that bring their necks under the yoke of the meleḵ of Baḇel and serve him, I shall leave in their own land,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and they shall till it and dwell in it.’ ”
27.12: And I spoke to Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ of Yahuḏah according to all these words, saying, “Bring your necks under the yoke of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and serve him and his people, and live!
27.13: “Why should you die, you and your people, by the sword, by the scarcity of food, and by the pestilence, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken against the nation that does not serve the meleḵ of Baḇel?
27.14: “Do not listen to the words of the neḇi’im who speak to you, saying, ‘Do not serve the meleḵ of Baḇel,’ for they naḇa falsehood to you,
27.15: for I have not sent them,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “yet they naḇa falsehood in My Name, in order that I drive you out. Then you shall perish, you and the neḇi’im who naḇa to you.”
27.16: Then I spoke to the kohenim and to all this people, saying, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Do not listen to the words of your neḇi’im who naḇa to you, saying, “See, the vessels of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are brought back from Baḇel soon now,” for they naḇa falsehood to you.
27.17: ‘Do not listen to them. Serve the meleḵ of Baḇel, and live! Why should this city become a ruin?
27.18: ‘But if they are neḇi’im, and if the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with them, let them now make intercession to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, that the vessels which are left in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and in the house of the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and at Yerushalayim, shall not go to Baḇel.’
27.19: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts concerning the columns, and concerning the sea, and concerning the stands, and concerning the remainder of the vessels which are left in this city,
27.20: which Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel did not take, when he exiled Yeḵonyahu the son of Yahoyaqim, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, from Yerushalayim to Baḇel, and all the nobles of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim -
27.21: thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, concerning the vessels that remain in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and in the house of the meleḵ of Yahuḏah and of Yerushalayim:
27.22: ‘They shall be brought to Baḇel, and be there until the day that I visit them,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. ‘Then I shall bring them back and restore them to this place.’ ”

28.1: And it came to be in that year, at the beginning of the reign of Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, in the fourth year and in the fifth month, that Ḥananyah son of Azzur the naḇi, who was from Giḇ’on, spoke to me in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the presence of the kohenim and of all the people, saying,
28.2: “Thus spoke 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘I have broken the yoke of the meleḵ of Baḇel.
28.3: Within two years I am going to bring back to this place all the vessels of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel removed from this place and took to Baḇel.
28.4: ‘And I am going to bring back to this place Yeḵonyahu son of Yahoyaqim, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, with all the exiles of Yahuḏah who went to Baḇel,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘for I am going to break the yoke of the meleḵ of Baḇel.’ ”
28.5: Then the naḇi Yirmeyahu spoke to the naḇi Ḥananyah in the presence of the kohenim and in the presence of all the people who stood in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
28.6: and the naḇi Yirmeyahu said, “Amĕn! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 do so! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 establish your words which you have naḇu, to bring back the vessels of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and all the exiles from Baḇel to this place!
28.7: “Only, hear now this word that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people:
28.8: “The neḇi’im who have been before me and before you of old naḇu against many lands and great reigns, of battle and of evil and of pestilence.
28.9: “The naḇi who naḇa of peace - when the word of the naḇi comes to pass, that naḇi is known as one whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has truly sent.”
28.10: And Ḥananyah the naḇi took the yoke off the naḇi Yirmeyahu’s neck and broke it.
28.11: And Ḥananyah spoke in the presence of all the people, saying, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘So I shall break the yoke of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel from the neck of all nations within two years.’ ” And the naḇi Yirmeyahu went his way.
28.12: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu, after Ḥananyah the naḇi had broken the yoke from the neck of the naḇi Yirmeyahu, saying,
28.13: “Go and speak to Ḥananyah, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “You have broken the yokes of wood, but you shall make yokes of iron instead.”
28.14: ‘For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations, to serve Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel. And they shall serve him. And I have also given him the beasts of the field.” ’ ”
28.15: And the naḇi Yirmeyahu said to Ḥananyah the naḇi, “Listen, please, Ḥananyah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not sent you, but you have made this people trust in falsehood.
28.16: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I am sending you away from the face of the earth. This year you shall die, for you have spoken apostasy against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”
28.17: And Ḥananyah the naḇi died the same year, in the seventh month.

29.1: And these are the words of the letter which Yirmeyahu the naḇi sent from Yerushalayim to the rest of the elders of the exile, and to the kohenim, and to the neḇi’im and to all the people whom Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had exiled from Yerushalayim to Baḇel -
29.2: after Yeḵonyah the meleḵ, and the queen mother, and the eunuchs, and the heads of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, and the craftsmen, and the smiths had gone from Yerushalayim -
29.3: by the hand of El’asah son of Shaphan, and Gemaryah the son of Ḥilqiyahu, whom Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah sent to Baḇel, to Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel, saying,
29.4: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, to all the exiles whom I exiled from Yerushalayim to Baḇel,
29.5: ‘Build houses and dwell, plant gardens and eat their fruit.
