29.6: ‘Take wives and bring forth sons and daughters. And take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, and let them bear sons and daughters, and be increased there, and not diminished.
29.7: ‘And seek the peace of the city where I have exiled you, and pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for it, for in its peace you have peace.’
29.8: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Let not your neḇi’im and your diviners who are in your midst deceive you, neither listen to the dreams which you are dreaming.
29.9: ‘For they naḇa falsely to you in My Name. I have not sent them,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
29.10: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘When seventy years are completed, at Baḇel I shall visit you and establish My good word toward you, to bring you back to this place.
29.11: ‘For I know the plans I am planning for you,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘plans of peace and not of evil, to give you an expectancy and a latter end.
29.12: ‘Then you shall call on Me, and shall come and pray to Me, and I shall listen to you.
29.13: ‘And you shall seek, and shall find Me, when you search for Me with all your heart.
29.14: ‘And I shall be found by you,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and I shall turn back your captivity, and shall gather you from all the gentiles and from all the places where I have driven you, declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And I shall bring you back to the place from which I have exiled you.’
29.15: “Because you have said, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has raised up neḇi’im for us in Baḇel’ -
29.16: thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning the meleḵ who sits on the throne of Dawiḏ, concerning all the people who dwell in this city, and concerning your brothers who have not gone out with you into exile,
29.17: thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, ‘See, I am sending on them the sword, the scarcity of food, and the pestilence. And I shall make them like spoilt figs, so spoilt as to be inedible.
29.18: ‘And I shall pursue them with the sword, with scarcity of food, and with pestilence. And I shall make them a horror among all the reigns of the earth, to be a curse, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach among all the gentiles where I have driven them.
29.19: ‘For they did not heed My words,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘which I sent to them by My servants the neḇi’im, rising up early and sending them, yet you did not listen,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
29.20: “You, therefore, hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all you exiles whom I have sent from Yerushalayim to Baḇel.
29.21: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, concerning Aḥaḇ son of Qolayah, and Tsiḏqiyahu son of Ma’asĕyah, who are naḇa falsely to you in My Name, ‘See, I am giving them into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, and he shall smite them before your eyes.
29.22: ‘And because of them all the exiles of Yahuḏah who are in Baḇel shall use a curse, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 make you like Tsiḏqiyahu and Aḥaḇ, whom the meleḵ of Baḇel roasted in the fire,”
29.23: because they have done wickedness in Yisra’ĕl, and committed adultery with their neighbors’ wives, and have spoken a word in My Name falsely which I have not commanded them. And I am He who knows, and a witness,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
29.24: “And speak to Shemayahu the Neḥelamite, saying,
29.25: “Thus speaks 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Because you have sent letters in your name to all the people who are at Yerushalayim, to Tsephanyah son of Ma’asĕyah the kohĕn, and to all the kohenim, saying,
29.26: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has made you kohĕn instead of Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn, so that there are overseers in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 over everyone who is mad and makes himself a naḇi, that you should put him in the stocks and in the iron collar.
29.27: “So why have you not reproved Yirmeyahu of Anathoth who makes himself a naḇi to you?
29.28: “For he has sent to us in Baḇel, saying, ‘This is long - build houses and dwell, and plant gardens and eat their fruit.’ ” ’ ”
29.29: And Tsephanyah the kohĕn read this letter in the hearing of Yirmeyahu the naḇi.
29.30: Then the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
29.31: “Send to all those in exile, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning Shemayah the Neḥelamite, “Because Shemayah has naḇu to you, and I have not sent him, and he has made you to trust on falsehood,”
29.32: therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am bringing punishment upon Shemayah the Neḥelamite and his seed: he shall have no one to dwell among this people, nor is he to see the good that I am about to do for My people,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “because he has spoken apostasy against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” ’ ”

3.1: saying, “If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him and becomes another man’s, does he return to her again? Would not that land be made greatly unclean? But you have committed whoring with many lovers. And would you return to Me?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.2: “Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and see: where have you not lain with men? Beside the ways you have sat for them like an Araḇian in the wilderness. And you made the land unclean with your whorings and your evil.
3.3: “Therefore the showers have been withheld, and there has been no latter rain. You have had a whore’s forehead, you refuse to be ashamed.
3.4: “Shall you not from now on cry to Me, ‘My father, You are the guide of my youth?
3.5: ‘Does one bear a grudge forever? Does one keep it to the end?’ See, you have spoken and done the evils that you could.”
3.6: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me in the days of Yoshiyahu the meleḵ, “Have you seen what backsliding Yisra’ĕl has done? She has gone up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and there committed whoring.
3.7: “And after she had done all these, I said ‘Return to Me.’ But she did not return. And her treacherous sister Yahuḏah saw it.
3.8: “And I saw that for all the causes for which backsliding Yisra’ĕl had committed adultery, I had put her away and given her a certificate of divorce; yet her treacherous sister Yahuḏah did not reverence, but went and committed whoring too.
3.9: “And it came to be, through her frivolous whoring, that she defiled the land and committed adultery with stones and wood.
3.10: “And yet for all this her treacherous sister Yahuḏah has not turned to Me with all her heart, but falsely,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, “Backsliding Yisra’ĕl has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Yahuḏah.
3.12: “Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, O backsliding Yisra’ĕl,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘I shall not look on you in displeasure, for I am kind,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and I do not bear a grudge forever.
3.13: ‘Only, acknowledge your wickedness, because you have transgressed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and have scattered your ways to strangers under every green tree, and you have not obeyed My voice,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.14: “Return, O backsliding children,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “for I shall rule over you, and shall take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and shall bring you to Tsiyon.
3.15: “And I shall give you shepherds according to My heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.
3.16: “And it shall be, when you have increased, and shall bear fruit in the land in those days, declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that they no longer say, ‘The ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ Neither would it come to heart, nor would they remember it, nor would they visit it, nor would it be made again.
3.17: “At that time Yerushalayim shall be called the throne of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to Yerushalayim, and no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.
3.18: “In those days the house of Yahuḏah shall go to the house of Yisra’ĕl, and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given as an inheritance to your fathers.
3.19: “But I said, ‘How would I put you among the children and give you a pleasant land, a splendid inheritance of the hosts of nations?’ ” And I said, ‘Call Me, “My Father,” and do not turn away from Me.’
3.20: “But indeed as a wife betrays her husband, so have you betrayed Me, O house of Yisra’ĕl,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.21: A voice was heard on the bare heights, weeping supplications of the children of Yisra’ĕl, because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim.
3.22: “Return, O backsliding children, I shall make your backslidings cease.” “See, we have come to You, for You are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.
3.23: “Truly, delusion comes from the high hills, the noisy throng on the mountains. Truly, in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim is the deliverance of Yisra’ĕl.
3.24: “For shame has devoured the labor of our fathers from our youth, their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.
3.25: “We shall lie down in our shame, while our reproach covers us. For we have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day, and have not obeyed the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.”

30.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
30.2: “Thus spoke 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Write in a book for yourself all the words that I have spoken to you.
30.3: ‘For look, the days are coming,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘when I shall turn back the captivity of My people Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and I shall bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers, and let them possess it.’ ”
30.4: And these are the words 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke concerning Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah.
30.5: “For this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, ‘We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.
30.6: ‘Ask now, and see if a man is giving birth. Why do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor, and all faces turned pale?
30.7: ‘Oh! For great is that day, there is none like it. And it is the time of Ya’aqoḇ’s distress, but he shall be saved out of it.
30.8: ‘And it shall be in that day,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, ‘that I break his yoke from your neck, and tear off your bonds, and foreigners no more enslave them.
30.9: ‘And they shall serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim and Dawiḏ their meleḵ, whom I raise up for them.
30.10: ‘And you, do not fear, O Ya’aqoḇ My servant,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘nor be discouraged, O Yisra’ĕl. For look, I am saving you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity. And Ya’aqoḇ shall return, and have rest and be at ease, with no one to trouble him.
30.11: ‘For I am with you,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘to save you. Though I make a complete end of all gentiles where I have scattered you, yet I do not make a complete end of you. But I shall reprove you in judgment, and by no means leave you unpunished.’
30.12: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Your breach is incurable, your wound is grievous.
30.13: ‘No one pleads your cause, to bind up. There are no healing medicines for you.
30.14: ‘All those loving you have forgotten you, they do not seek you. For I smote you as an enemy smites, with cruel chastisement, because your wickedness is great, your sins have increased.
30.15: ‘Why do you cry about your breach? Your pain is incurable. Because of your many wickednesses, because your sins have increased, I have done this to you.
30.16: ‘However, all those who devour you shall be devoured. And all your adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity. And those who exploit you shall be exploited, and all who prey upon you I shall make a prey.
30.17: ‘For I restore health to you and heal you of your wounds,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘for they have called you an outcast saying, “This is Tsiyon, no one is seeking her.” ’
30.18: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I turn back the captivity of Ya’aqoḇ’s tents, and have compassion on his dwelling places. And the city shall be built upon its own mound, and the palace stand on its right place.
30.19: ‘And out of them shall arise thanksgiving and the voice of those who are laughing. And I shall increase them, and they shall not diminish. And I shall esteem them, and they shall not be small.
30.20: ‘And his children shall be as before, and his congregation shall be established before Me. And I shall punish all who oppress them.
30.21: ‘And his Prince shall be from him, and his Ruler shall come from among him. And I shall bring him near, and he shall approach Me, for who is this who pledged his heart to approach Me?’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
30.22: ‘And you shall be My people, and I shall be your Elohim.’ ”
30.23: See, the storm of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall go forth in a rage, a whirling storm! It bursts upon the head of the wicked.
30.24: The burning displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall not turn back until He has done and established the purposes of His heart. In the latter days you shall understand it.

31.1: “At that time,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I shall be the Elohim of all the clans of Yisra’ĕl, and they shall be My people.”
31.2: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “A people escaped from the sword found favor in the wilderness, Yisra’ĕl, when it went to find rest.”
31.3: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to me from afar, “I have loved you with an everlasting love, therefore I shall draw you with kindness.
31.4: “I am going to build you again. And you shall be rebuilt, O maiden of Yisra’ĕl! Again you shall take up your tambourines, and go forth in the dances of those who rejoice.
31.5: “Again you shall plant vines on the mountains of Shomeron. The planters shall plant and treat them as common.
31.6: “For there shall be a day when the watchmen cry on Mount Ephrayim, ‘Arise, and let us go up to Tsiyon, to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.’ ”
31.7: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Sing with gladness for Ya’aqoḇ, and shout among the chief of the nations. Cry out, give praise, and say, ‘O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, save Your people, the remnant of Yisra’ĕl!’
31.8: “See, I am bringing them from the land of the north, and shall gather them from the ends of the earth, among them the blind and the lame, those with child and those in labor, together - a great assembly returning here.
31.9: “With weeping they shall come, and with prayers I bring them. I shall make them walk by rivers of waters, in a straight way in which they do not stumble. For I shall be a Father to Yisra’ĕl, and Ephrayim - he is My first-born.
31.10: “Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O gentiles, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, ‘He who scattered Yisra’ĕl gathers him, and shall guard him as a shepherd, his flock.’
31.11: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall ransom Ya’aqoḇ, and redeem him from the hand of one stronger than he.
31.12: “And they shall come in and shall sing on the height of Tsiyon, and flow toward the goodness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for grain and for new wine and for oil, and for the young of the flock and the herd. And their being shall be like a well-watered garden, and never languish again.
31.13: “Then shall a maiden rejoice in a dance, and young men and old, together. And I shall turn their mourning to joy, and shall comfort them, and shall make them rejoice from their sorrow,
31.14: and shall fill the being of the kohenim with fatness. And My people shall be satisfied with My goodness,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.15: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing, bitter weeping, Raḥĕl weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.”
31.16: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Hold back your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and they shall return from the land of the enemy.
31.17: “And there is expectancy for your latter end,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and your children shall return to their own country.
31.18: “I have clearly heard Ephrayim lamenting, ‘You have chastised me, and I was chastised, like an untrained calf. Turn me back, and I shall turn back, for You are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim.
31.19: ‘For after my turning back, I repented. And after I was instructed, I struck myself on the thigh. I was ashamed, even humiliated, for I bore the reproach of my youth.’
31.20: “Is Ephrayim a precious son to Me, a child of delights? For though I spoke against him, I still remembered him. That is why My affections were deeply moved for him. I have great compassion for him,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.21: “Put up signposts, make landmarks; lay your heart toward the highway, the way in which you went. Turn back, O maiden of Yisra’ĕl, turn back to these cities of yours!
31.22: “Till when would you turn here and there, O backsliding daughter? For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has created what is new on earth: a woman encompasses a man!”
31.23: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Let them once again say this word in the land of Yahuḏah and in its cities, when I turn back their captivity, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 baraḵ you, O home of righteousness, mountain of qodeshah!’
31.24: “And in Yahuḏah and all its cities farmers and those who journey with flocks, shall dwell together.
31.25: “For I shall fill the weary being, and I shall replenish every grieved being.”
31.26: At this I awoke and looked around, and my sleep was sweet to me.
31.27: “See, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that I shall sow the house of Yisra’ĕl and the house of Yahuḏah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.
31.28: “And it shall be, that as I have watched over them to pluck up, and to break down, and to throw down, and to destroy, and to afflict, so I shall watch over them to build and to plant,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.29: “In those days they shall no longer say, ‘The fathers ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are blunted.’
31.30: “But each one shall die for his own wickedness - whoever eats sour grapes, his teeth shall be blunted.
31.31: “See, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when I shall make a new Covenant with the house of Yisra’ĕl and with the house of Yahuḏah,
31.32: not like the Covenant I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Mitsrayim, My Covenant which they broke, though I was a husband to them,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.33: “For this is the Covenant I shall make with the house of Yisra’ĕl after those days, declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: I shall put My Torah in their inward parts, and write it on their hearts. And I shall be their Elohim, and they shall be My people.
31.34: “And no longer shall they teach, each one his neighbor, and each one his brother, saying, ‘Know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,’ for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “For I shall forgive their wickedness, and remember their sin no more.”
31.35: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who gives the sun for a light by day, and the laws of the moon and the stars for a light by night, who stirs up the sea, and its waves roar - 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts is His Name:
31.36: “If these laws vanish from before Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “then the seed of Yisra’ĕl shall also cease from being a nation before Me forever.”
31.37: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “If the shamayim above could be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I would also cast off all the seed of Yisra’ĕl for all that they have done,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.38: “See, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that the city shall be built for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from the Tower of Ḥanane’ĕl to the Corner Gate.
31.39: “And the measuring line shall again extend straight ahead to the hill Garĕḇ, then it shall turn toward Go’ah.
31.40: “And all the valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields as far as the wadi Qiḏron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, is to be qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It shall not be plucked up or thrown down any more forever.”

32.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the tenth year of Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, which was the eighteenth year of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar.
32.2: Now at that time the army of the meleḵ of Baḇel besieged Yerushalayim, and Yirmeyahu the naḇi was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the house of the meleḵ of Yahuḏah.
32.3: For Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah had shut him up, saying, “Why do you neḇuah, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am giving this city into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and he shall take it,
32.4: and Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah shall not escape from the hand of the Kasdites, but certainly be given into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and shall speak with him face to face, and see him eye to eye,
32.5: and he shall lead Tsiḏqiyahu to Baḇel, and be there until I visit him,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “though you fight with the Kasdites, you shall not prosper” ’?”
32.6: And Yirmeyahu said, “The word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
32.7: ‘See, Ḥaname’ĕl son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you saying, “Buy my field which is in Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.” ’
32.8: “So Ḥaname’ĕl my uncle’s son came to me in the court of the guard according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said to me, ‘Please buy my field that is in Anathoth, which is in the land of Binyamin, for the right of inheritance is yours, and the redemption. Buy it for yourself.’ And I knew that this was the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
32.9: “And I bought the field which was at Anathoth from Ḥaname’ĕl, my uncle’s son, and weighed out to him the silver, seventeen sheqels of silver.
32.10: “And I signed the deed and sealed it, took witnesses, and weighed the silver in the scales.
32.11: “Then I took the deed of purchase - that which was sealed according to the command and law, and that which was open -
32.12: and I gave the deed of purchase to Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah, son of Maḥsĕyah, in the presence of Ḥaname’ĕl my uncle’s son, and in the presence of the witnesses who signed the deed of purchase, before all the Yahuḏim who sat in the court of the guard.
32.13: “And I commanded Baruḵ before their eyes, saying,
32.14: ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Take these deeds, both this deed of purchase which is sealed and this deed which is open, and put them in an earthen vessel, so that they remain many days.”
32.15: ‘For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Houses and fields and vineyards shall again be bought in this land.” ’
32.16: “And after I had given the deed of purchase to Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah, I prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
32.17: ‘Ah, Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! See, You have made the shamayim and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm. There is no matter too hard for You,
32.18: who show kindness to thousands, and repay the wickedness of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them - the Great, the Mighty Ĕl, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts is His Name,
32.19: great in counsel and mighty in work, for Your eyes are open to all the ways of the sons of men, to give everyone according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
32.20: ‘For You have put signs and wonders in the land of Mitsrayim, to this day, and in Yisra’ĕl and among other men. And You have made Yourself a Name, as it is this day.
32.21: ‘And You have brought Your people Yisra’ĕl out of the land of Mitsrayim with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great fearsome deeds.
32.22: ‘And You gave them this land, of which You swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
32.23: ‘And they came in and possessed it, but they did not obey Your voice nor did they walk in Your Torah. They did not do all that You commanded them to do, so You brought all this evil upon them.
32.24: ‘See the siege mounds! They have come to the city to take it. And the city has been given into the hand of the Kasdites who fight against it, because of the sword and the scarcity of food and the pestilence. And what You have spoken has come about, and look, You see it!
32.25: ‘Yet You, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, have said to me, “Buy the field for silver, and take witnesses”! although the city has been given into the hand of the Kasdites.’ ”
32.26: Then the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
32.27: “See, I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of all flesh. Is there any matter too hard for Me?”
32.28: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am giving this city into the hand of the Kasdites, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, and he shall take it.
32.29: “And the Kasdites who fight against this city shall come and light fire to this city and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Ba’al and poured out drink offerings to other mighty ones, to provoke Me.
32.30: “For the children of Yisra’ĕl and the children of Yahuḏah have done only evil before Me, from their youth. For the children of Yisra’ĕl have only provoked Me with the work of their hands,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
32.31: “For this city has been a cause for My displeasure and My wrath from the day that they built it, even to this day that I should remove it from before My face,
32.32: because of all the evil of the children of Yisra’ĕl and the children of Yahuḏah, which they have done to provoke Me - they, their melaḵim, their heads, their kohenim, their neḇi’im, and the men of Yahuḏah, and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
32.33: “And they have turned their back to Me, and not their face - though I taught them, rising up early and teaching them, they did not listen to receive instruction.
32.34: “And they put their abominations in the House which is called by My Name, to defile it.
32.35: “And they built the high places of Ba’al which are in the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, to offer up their sons and their daughters to Moleḵ, which I did not command them, nor did it come into My heart, that they should do this abomination, to make Yahuḏah sin.
32.36: “And now, thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, concerning this city of which you say, ‘It shall be given into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel by the sword, and by scarcity of food, and by pestilence’:
32.37: ‘See, I am gathering them out of all the lands where I have driven them in My displeasure, and in My wrath, and in great rage. And I shall bring them back to this place, and shall let them dwell in safety.
32.38: ‘And they shall be My people, and I shall be their Elohim.
32.39: ‘And I shall give them one heart and one Way, to revere Me all the days, for the good of them and of their children after them.
32.40: ‘And I shall make an everlasting Covenant with them, that I do not turn back from doing good to them. And I shall put My reverence in their hearts so as not to turn aside from Me.
32.41: ‘And I shall rejoice over them to do good to them, and shall plant them in this land in truth, with all My heart and with all My being.’
32.42: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘As I have brought all this great evil on this people, so I am bringing on them all the good that I am speaking to them.
32.43: ‘And fields shall be bought in this land of which you are saying, “It is a wasteland, without man or beast. It has been given into the hand of the Kasdites.”
32.44: ‘Fields shall be bought for silver, and deeds signed and sealed, and witnesses be called, in the land of Binyamin, and in the places around Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yahuḏah, and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the low country, and in the cities of the Negeḇ. For I shall turn back their captivity,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

33.1: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu a second time, while he was still shut up in the court of the guard, saying,
33.2: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who made it, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who formed it to establish it, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is His Name,
33.3: ‘Call unto Me, and I shall answer you, and show you greatness and unknowns, which you have not known.’
33.4: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah, which are thrown down against the siege mounds and the sword,
33.5: while coming to fight with the Kasdites, and to fill their places with the corpses of men whom I shall slay in My displeasure and My wrath, all for whose evil I have hidden My face from this city.
33.6: ‘See, I am bringing to it relief and healing. And I shall heal them and reveal to them the riches of peace and truth.
33.7: ‘And I shall turn back the captivity of Yahuḏah and the captivity of Yisra’ĕl, and shall build them as at the first,
33.8: and shall cleanse them from all their wickedness that they have sinned against Me. And I shall pardon all their wickednesses that they have sinned and by which they have transgressed against Me.
33.9: ‘And it shall be to Me a name of joy, a praise, and a pride before all nations of the earth, who hear all the good I am doing to them, and they shall revere and quiver for all the goodness and all the peace I am doing to it.’
33.10: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘In this place of which you say, “It is dried up, without man and without beast,” in the cities of Yahuḏah, in the streets of Yerushalayim that are deserted, without man and without inhabitant and without beast, there shall once again be heard
33.11: the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who are saying, “Praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is good, for His kindness is forever,” of those who are bringing the offering of praise into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. For I shall turn back the captivity of the land, as at the first,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
33.12: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, ‘In this place which is dried up, without man and without beast, and in all its cities, there shall once again be a home of shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.
33.13: ‘In the cities of the mountains, in the cities of the low country, and in the cities of the Negeḇ, and in the land of Binyamin, and in the places around Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yahuḏah, the flocks once again pass under the hands of him who counts them,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
33.14: ‘See, the days are coming,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘when I shall establish the good word which I have promised to the house of Yisra’ĕl and to the house of Yahuḏah:
33.15: ‘In those days and at that time I cause a Branch of righteousness to spring forth for Dawiḏ. And He shall do right-ruling and righteousness in the earth.
33.16: ‘In those days Yahuḏah shall be saved, and Yerushalayim dwell in safety. And this is that which shall be proclaimed to her: ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Righteousness.’
33.17: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘For Dawiḏ there is not to cease a man to sit on the throne of the house of Yisra’ĕl.
33.18: ‘And for the kohenim, the Lĕwites, there is not to cease a man to offer burnt offerings before Me, to kindle grain offerings, and to slaughter continually.’ ”
33.19: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
33.20: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘If you could break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, so that there be not day and night in their season,
33.21: then My covenant could also be broken with Dawiḏ My servant - so that he shall not have a son to reign upon his throne - and with the Lĕwites, the kohenim, My attendants.
33.22: ‘As the host of the shamayim is not counted, nor the sand of the sea measured, so I increase the descendants of Dawiḏ My servant and the Lĕwites who attend upon Me.’ ”
33.23: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
33.24: “Have you not observed what these people have spoken, saying, ‘The two clans which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen have been rejected by Him’? So they have despised My people, no more to be a nation before them.
33.25: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘If My covenant is not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the laws of the shamayim and earth,
33.26: then I would also reject the descendants of Ya’aqoḇ and Dawiḏ My servant, so that I should not take of his descendants to be rulers over the descendants of Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya’aqoḇ. For I shall turn back their captivity, and have compassion on them.’ ”

34.1: The word which came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, when Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel and all his army, and all the reigns of the earth under his rule, and all the people, fought against Yerushalayim and all its cities, saying,
34.2: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Go and speak to Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah and say to him, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I am giving this city into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel. And he shall burn it with fire,
34.3: and you shall not escape out of his hand, but certainly be taken and given into his hand. And your eyes shall see the eyes of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and his mouth shall speak with your mouth, and you shall go to Baḇel.’ ” ’
34.4: “But hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah! Thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said concerning you, ‘You shall not die by the sword.
34.5: ‘In peace you are to die, and as in the burnings of spices for your fathers, the former melaḵim who were before you, so they shall burn spices for you and lament for you, saying, “Alas, master!” ’ For I have spoken the word,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
34.6: And Yirmeyahu the naḇi spoke all these words to Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ of Yahuḏah in Yerushalayim,
34.7: while the meleḵ of Baḇel’s army was fighting against Yerushalayim and all the cities of Yahuḏah that were left, against Laḵish and Azĕqah. For only these walled cities remained of the cities of Yahuḏah.
34.8: The word which came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, after Meleḵ Tsiḏqiyahu had made a covenant with all the people who were at Yerushalayim to proclaim release to them:
34.9: that everyone was to let his male and female slave go free, the Iḇri man and the Iḇri woman, no one was to keep a Yahuḏi, his brother, enslaved.
34.10: And when all the heads and all the people who had come into the covenant heard that each one was to let his male and female slaves go free, and not keep them enslaved any longer, they obeyed and released them.
34.11: But afterward they changed their minds and made the male and female slaves return, whom they had let go free, and brought them into subjection as male and female slaves.
34.12: Therefore the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
34.13: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘I Myself made a Covenant with your fathers in the day that I brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, out of the house of bondage, saying,
34.14: “At the end of seven years each one should let his Iḇri brother go free, who has been sold to him. And when he has served you six years, you shall let him go free from you.” But your fathers did not obey Me nor incline their ear.
34.15: ‘And you recently turned and did what was right in My eyes, each man proclaiming release to his neighbor. And you made a covenant before Me in the House which is called by My Name.
34.16: ‘But you turned back and profaned My Name, and each one of you took back his male and female slaves, whom he had let go free, at their pleasure, and brought them into subjection, to be your male and female slaves.’
34.17: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘You have not obeyed Me in proclaiming release, each one to his brother and each one to his neighbor. See, I am proclaiming release to you,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the scarcity of food! And I shall make you a horror to all reigns of the earth.
34.18: ‘And I shall give the men who are transgressing My Covenant, who have not established the words of the covenant which they made before Me, when they cut the calf in two and passed between the parts of it:
34.19: the heads of Yahuḏah, and the heads of Yerushalayim, the eunuchs, and the kohenim, and all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf.
34.20: ‘And I shall give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life. And their corpses shall be for food to the birds of the shamayim and the beasts of the earth.
34.21: ‘And I shall give Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah and his heads into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel’s army that has withdrawn from you.
34.22: ‘See, I am commanding,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘and shall bring them back to this city, and they shall fight against it and take it and burn it with fire. And I shall make the cities of Yahuḏah a ruin without inhabitant.’ ”

35.1: The word which came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the days of Yahoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, saying,
35.2: “Go to the house of the Rĕḵaḇites. And you shall speak to them, and bring them into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, into one of the rooms, and give them wine to drink.”
35.3: And I took Ya’azanyah the son of Yirmeyahu, the son of Ḥaḇatstsinyah, and his brothers and all his sons, and all the house of the Rĕḵaḇites,
35.4: and brought them into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, into the room of the sons of Ḥanan son of Yiḡdalyahu, a man of Elohim, which was by the chamber of the heads, above the room of Ma’asĕyahu son of Shallum, the keeper of the door.
35.5: And I put before the sons of the house of the Rĕḵaḇites bowls filled with wine, and cups, and I said to them, “Drink wine.”
35.6: But they said, “We do not drink wine, because Yonaḏaḇ the son of Rĕḵaḇ, our father, commanded us, saying, ‘You shall not drink wine, neither you nor your sons, forever.
35.7: ‘And do not build a house, neither sow seed, nor plant a vineyard, nor have any of these, but dwell in tents all your days, so that you live many days on the face of the land where you are sojourners.’
35.8: “So we obeyed the voice of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rĕḵaḇ, our father, in all that he commanded us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters,
35.9: nor to build ourselves houses to dwell in. And we have no vineyard, field or seed.
35.10: “But we dwell in tents, and have obeyed and done according to all that Yonaḏaḇ our father commanded us.
35.11: “And it came to be, when Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel came up into the land, that we said, ‘Come, let us go to Yerushalayim for fear of the army of the Kasdites and for fear of the army of the Arameans.’ So we dwell at Yerushalayim.”
35.12: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
35.13: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Go, and you shall say to the men of Yahuḏah and to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, “Have you not received instruction, to obey My Words?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
35.14: “The words of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rĕḵaḇ, which he commanded his sons, not to drink wine, are established, and they have not drunk unto this day, for they have obeyed their father’s command. And as for Me, I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, but you have not obeyed Me.
35.15: “And I sent to you all My servants the neḇi’im, rising up early and sending them, saying, ‘Turn, each one from his evil way, and make good your deeds, and do not go after other mighty ones to serve them, and you shall dwell in the land which I have given you and your fathers.’ But you have not inclined your ear, nor obeyed Me.
35.16: “The sons of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rĕḵaḇ have indeed carried out the command of their father which he commanded them, but this people has not obeyed Me.’ ”
35.17: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘See, I am bringing on Yahuḏah and on all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim all the evil I have pronounced against them, because I have spoken to them but they did not listen, and I have called to them but they did not answer.’ ”
35.18: And Yirmeyahu said to the house of the Rĕḵaḇites, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Because you have obeyed the command of Yonaḏaḇ your father, and guarded all his commands and done according to all that he commanded you,
35.19: therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Of Yonaḏaḇ son of Rĕḵaḇ there shall never cease to be a man to stand before Me.” ’ ”

36.1: And it came to be in the fourth year of Yahoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, that this word came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
36.2: “Take a scroll and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you against Yisra’ĕl, and against Yahuḏah, and against all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Yoshiyahu even to this day.
36.3: “It could be that the house of Yahuḏah hears of all the evil which I plan to bring upon them, so that each one turns back from his evil way, and I shall pardon their wickedness and their sin.”
36.4: And Yirmeyahu called Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah. And Baruḵ wrote on a scroll from the mouth of Yirmeyahu, all the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He had spoken to him.
36.5: And Yirmeyahu commanded Baruḵ, saying, “I am shut up, I am unable to enter the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
36.6: “But you shall enter, and shall read from the scroll which you have written from my mouth, the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in the hearing of the people in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the day of fasting. And also read them in the hearing of all Yahuḏah who come from their cities.
36.7: “It could be that they present their supplication before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and they turn back, each one from his evil way. For great is the displeasure and the wrath that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken against this people.”
36.8: And Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah did according to all that Yirmeyahu the naḇi commanded him, reading from the book the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
36.9: And it came to be in the fifth year of Yahoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, in the ninth month, that they called a fast before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to all the people in Yerushalayim, and to all the people who came from the cities of Yahuḏah to Yerushalayim.
36.10: And Baruḵ read from the book the words of Yirmeyahu in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in the room of Gemaryahu son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard at the entry of the New Gate of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in the hearing of all the people.
36.11: And Miḵayahu son of Gemaryahu, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from the book.
36.12: And then he went down to the meleḵ’s house, into the scribe’s room. And there all the heads were sitting: Elishama the scribe, Delayahu son of Shemayahu, Elnathan son of Aḵbor, Gemaryahu son of Shaphan, Tsiḏqiyahu son of Ḥananyahu, and all the heads.
36.13: And Miḵayahu told them all the words which he heard when Baruḵ read the book in the hearing of the people.
36.14: Then all the heads sent Yahuḏi son of Nethanyahu, son of Shelemyahu, son of Kushi, to Baruḵ, saying, “Take in your hand the scroll from which you have read in the hearing of the people, and come.” So Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
36.15: And they said to him, “Sit down, please, and read it in our hearing.” Then Baruḵ read it in their hearing.
36.16: And it came to be, when they had heard all the words, that they looked at each other in fear, and said to Baruḵ, “We are certainly going to report all these words to the meleḵ.”
36.17: And they asked Baruḵ, saying, “Please explain to us, how did you write all these words? From his mouth?”
36.18: And Baruḵ answered them, “From his mouth he spoke all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink in the book.”
36.19: Then the heads said to Baruḵ, “Go, hide, you and Yirmeyahu, and let no one know where you are.”
36.20: And they went to the meleḵ, into the court. But they put the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe, and told all the words in the hearing of the meleḵ.
36.21: The meleḵ therefore sent Yahuḏi to bring the scroll, and he took it from the room of Elishama the scribe. And Yahuḏi read it in the hearing of the meleḵ and in the hearing of all the heads standing beside the meleḵ.
36.22: And the meleḵ was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a fire burning on the hearth before him.
36.23: Then it came to be, when Yahuḏi had read three or four columns, that the meleḵ cut it with the scribe’s knife and threw it into the fire that was on the hearth, until the entire scroll was burned in the fire that was on the hearth.
36.24: Yet the meleḵ and all his servants who heard all these words were not afraid, nor did they tear their garments.
36.25: Moreover, Elnathan, and Delayahu, and Gemaryahu pleaded with the meleḵ not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them.
36.26: And the meleḵ commanded Yeraḥme’ĕl son of the meleḵ, and Serayahu son of Azri’ĕl, and Shelemyahu son of Aḇde’ĕl, to seize Baruḵ the scribe and Yirmeyahu the naḇi, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had hid them.
36.27: And after the meleḵ had burned the scroll with the words which Baruḵ had written from the mouth of Yirmeyahu, the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
36.28: “Take another scroll, and write on it all the former words that were in the first scroll which Yahoyaqim the meleḵ of Yahuḏah has burned,
36.29: and say to Yahoyaqim meleḵ of Yahuḏah, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “You have burned this scroll, saying, ‘Why have you written in it that the meleḵ of Baḇel is certainly coming to destroy this land, and cause man and beast to cease from here?’ ”
36.30: ‘Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning Yahoyaqim meleḵ of Yahuḏah, “He shall have no one to sit on the throne of Dawiḏ, and his dead body is to be thrown out, to the heat of the day and the frost of the night.
36.31: “And I shall punish him, and his seed, and his servants for their wickedness. And I shall bring on them, and on the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and on the men of Yahuḏah all the evil I have spoken against them. But they did not listen.” ’ ”
36.32: So Yirmeyahu took another scroll and gave it to Baruḵ the scribe, son of Nĕriyah, who wrote on it from the mouth of Yirmeyahu all the words of the book which Yahoyaqim meleḵ of Yahuḏah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.

37.1: And Meleḵ Tsiḏqiyahu son of Yoshiyahu reigned instead of Konyahu son of Yahoyaqim, whom Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel appointed to reign in the land of Yahuḏah.
37.2: But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land had listened to the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He spoke by the naḇi Yirmeyahu.
37.3: And Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ sent Yahuḵal son of Shelemyah, and the kohĕn, Tsephanyahu son of Ma’asĕyah, to the naḇi Yirmeyahu, saying, “Please pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim for us.”
37.4: Now Yirmeyahu was still coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
37.5: Meanwhile, Pharaoh’s army had departed from Mitsrayim. And when the Kasdites who were besieging Yerushalayim heard news of them, they withdrew from Yerushalayim.
37.6: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu the naḇi, saying,
37.7: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Say this to the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, who sent you to Me to inquire of Me, “See, Pharaoh’s army which has come up to help you, shall turn back to Mitsrayim, to their own land.
37.8: “And the Kasdites shall return and fight against this city, and take it and burn it with fire.” ’
37.9: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Do not deceive yourselves, saying, “The Kasdites shall go away from us,” for they do not go.
37.10: ‘For though you had smitten the entire army of the Kasdites who are fighting against you, and there remained only wounded men among them, they would get up, each man in his tent, and burn the city with fire.’ ”
37.11: And it came to be, when the army of the Kasdites left the siege of Yerushalayim for fear of Pharaoh’s army,
37.12: that Yirmeyahu went out of Yerushalayim to go into the land of Binyamin to receive his portion there in the midst of the people.
37.13: And it came to be, as he was in the gate of Binyamin, a master of the guard was there whose name was Yiriyah son of Shelemyah, son of Ḥananyah. And he seized Yirmeyahu the naḇi, saying, “You are deserting to the Kasdites!”
37.14: But Yirmeyahu said, “It is a lie! I am not deserting to the Kasdites.” But he did not listen to him, and Yiriyah seized Yirmeyahu and brought him to the heads.
37.15: And the heads were wroth with Yirmeyahu, and smote him and put him in prison in the house of Yahonathan the scribe. For they had made that for a prison.
37.16: When Yirmeyahu had entered into the dungeon and into the cells, then Yirmeyahu remained there many days.
37.17: And Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ sent and took him out. And the meleḵ asked him secretly in his house, and said, “Is there any word from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?” And Yirmeyahu said, “There is.” And he said, “You are given into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel!”
37.18: And Yirmeyahu said to Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ, “What have I sinned against you, and against your servants, and against this people, that you have put me into prison?
37.19: “Where are your neḇi’im who naḇu to you, saying, ‘The meleḵ of Baḇel is not coming against you or against this land?’
37.20: “But now, please hear, O my master the meleḵ. Please, let my petition be accepted before you, and do not make me return to the house of Yahonathan the scribe, lest I die there.”
37.21: Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ then gave orders for Yirmeyahu to be placed in the court of the guard, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread from the bakers’ street, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Yirmeyahu remained in the court of the guard.

38.1: And Shephatyah son of Mattan, and Geḏalyahu son of Pashḥur, and Yuḵal son of Shelemyahu, and Pashḥur son of Malkiyah heard the words which Yirmeyahu had spoken to all the people, saying,
38.2: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘He who remains in this city shall die by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence, but whoever goes over to the Kasdites shall live. And his life shall be as a prize to him, and he shall live.’
38.3: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘This city is certainly given into the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel’s army, and he shall take it.’ ”
38.4: Then the heads said to the meleḵ, “Please, let this man be put to death, because he is weakening the hands of the men of battle who are left in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking such words to them. For this man does not seek the peace of this people, but the evil.”
38.5: And Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ said, “Look, he is in your hand. For the meleḵ is unable to do any matter against you.”
38.6: And they took Yirmeyahu and threw him into the dungeon of Malkiyahu the meleḵ’s son, which was in the court of the guard, and they let Yirmeyahu down with ropes. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mud. So Yirmeyahu sank in the mud.
38.7: And Eḇeḏ-Meleḵ the Kushite, one of the eunuchs, who was in the meleḵ’s house, heard that they had put Yirmeyahu in the dungeon. And the meleḵ was sitting at the Gate of Binyamin,
38.8: And Eḇeḏ-Meleḵ came from the meleḵ’s house and spoke to the meleḵ, saying,
38.9: “My master the meleḵ, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Yirmeyahu the naḇi, whom they have thrown into the dungeon, and he is likely to die from hunger in the place where he is, for there is no more bread in the city.”
38.10: And the meleḵ commanded Eḇeḏ-Meleḵ the Kushite, saying, “Take thirty men from here with you, and lift Yirmeyahu the naḇi out of the dungeon before he dies.”
38.11: So Eḇeḏ-Meleḵ took the men with him and went into the house of the meleḵ under the treasury, and took old clothes and old rags from there, and let them down by ropes into the dungeon to Yirmeyahu.
38.12: And Eḇeḏ-Meleḵ the Kushite said to Yirmeyahu, “Please put these old clothes and rags under your armpits, under the ropes.” And Yirmeyahu did so,
38.13: and they pulled Yirmeyahu up with ropes and lifted him out of the dungeon. And Yirmeyahu remained in the court of the guard.
38.14: Then Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ sent and had Yirmeyahu the naḇi brought to him at the third entrance of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And the meleḵ said to Yirmeyahu, “I am asking you a matter. Do not hide a matter from me.”
38.15: And Yirmeyahu said to Tsiḏqiyahu, “If I declare it to you, shall you not put me to death? And if I give you advice, you shall not listen to me.”
38.16: But Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ swore secretly to Yirmeyahu, saying, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, who made us this life, I do not put you to death, nor do I give you into the hand of these men who seek your life.”
38.17: And Yirmeyahu said to Tsiḏqiyahu, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘If you do indeed surrender to the heads of the meleḵ of Baḇel, then your being shall live, and this city not be burned with fire. And you and your house shall live.
38.18: ‘But if you do not surrender to the heads of the meleḵ of Baḇel, then this city shall be given into the hand of the Kasdites, and they shall burn it with fire, and you shall not escape from their hand.’ ”
38.19: Then Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ said to Yirmeyahu, “I am afraid of the Yahuḏim who have gone over to the Kasdites, lest they give me into their hand, and they maltreat me.”
38.20: But Yirmeyahu said, “They shall not hand you over. Please, obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which I speak to you, and let it be well with you, and your life be spared.
38.21: “But if you refuse to surrender, this is the word that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has shown me:
38.22: ‘Then see, all the women who are left in the meleḵ of Yahuḏah’s house shall be surrendered to the heads of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and see, they are saying, “Your close friends have provoked you and prevailed against you; your feet have sunk in the mire; they have turned away again.”
38.23: ‘And they are going to surrender all your wives and children to the Kasdites, and you yourself shall not escape from their hand, but be taken by the hand of the meleḵ of Baḇel, and this city shall be burned with fire.’ ”
38.24: Then Tsiḏqiyahu said to Yirmeyahu, “Let no one know of these words, and you shall not die.
38.25: “But if the heads hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, ‘Declare to us now what you have said to the meleḵ, and also what the meleḵ said to you. Do not hide it from us, and we do not put you to death,’
38.26: then you shall say to them, ‘I presented my petition before the meleḵ, not to send me back to the house of Yahonathan to die there.’ ”
38.27: And all the heads came to Yirmeyahu and asked him. And he informed them according to all these words that the meleḵ had commanded. And they said no more to him, for the matter was not heard.
38.28: So Yirmeyahu remained in the court of the guard until the day that Yerushalayim was taken, and he was when Yerushalayim was taken.

39.1: In the ninth year of Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, in the tenth month, Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel and all his army came against Yerushalayim, and besieged it.
39.2: In the eleventh year of Tsiḏqiyahu, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was broken into.
39.3: And all the heads of the meleḵ of Baḇel came in and sat in the Middle Gate: Nĕrḡal Sar-Etser, Samgar-Neḇo, Sarseḵim, Raḇsaris, Nĕrḡal Sar-Etser, Raḇmaḡ, and all the rest of the heads of the meleḵ of Baḇel.
39.4: And it came to be, when Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ of Yahuḏah and all the men of battle saw them, they fled and left the city by night, by way of the meleḵ’s garden, by the gate between the two walls. And he went out toward the desert plain.
39.5: But the army of the Kasdites pursued them and overtook Tsiḏqiyahu in the desert plains of Yeriḥo. And they captured him, and brought him up to Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, to Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath, where he spoke judgment on him.
39.6: And the meleḵ of Baḇel slew the sons of Tsiḏqiyahu before his eyes in Riḇlah. The meleḵ of Baḇel also slew all the nobles of Yahuḏah.
39.7: And he put out the eyes of Tsiḏqiyahu, and bound him with bronze shackles to bring him to Baḇel.
39.8: And the Kasdites burned the house of the meleḵ and the houses of the people with fire, and they broke down the walls of Yerushalayim.
39.9: And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, exiled to Baḇel the remnant of the people who remained in the city and those who defected to him, with the rest of the people who were left.
39.10: But Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, left in the land of Yahuḏah the poor people, who had naught whatever, and gave them vineyards and fields on the same day.
39.11: And Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel gave an order concerning Yirmeyahu to Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, saying,
39.12: “Take him and look after him, and do no harm whatsoever to him, but do to him even as he shall speak to you.”
39.13: And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, and Neḇushazban the Raḇsaris, Nĕrḡal Sar-Etser the Raḇmaḡ, and all the meleḵ of Baḇel’s chief officers sent,
39.14: and had Yirmeyahu taken from the court of the guard, and gave him to Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. And he dwelt among the people.
39.15: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had come to Yirmeyahu while he was shut up in the court of the guard, saying,
39.16: “Go, and you shall speak to Eḇeḏ-Meleḵ the Kushite, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “See, I am bringing My words upon this city for evil and not for good, and they shall be before you in that day.
39.17: “And I shall deliver you in that day,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “so that you are not given into the hand of the men of whom you are afraid.
39.18: “For I shall rescue you, and you shall not fall by the sword. But your life shall be as a prize to you, for you have put your trust in Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”

4.1: “If you do return, O Yisra’ĕl,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “return to Me. And if you remove your abominations from My presence, and cease straying,
4.2: and shall swear, ‘As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives,’ in truth, in right-ruling, and in righteousness - then nations shall baraḵ themselves in Him, and they shall boast in Him!”
4.3: For this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to the men of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, “Break up your tillable ground, and do not sow among thorns.
4.4: “Circumcise yourselves unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and take away the foreskins of your hearts, you men of Yahuḏah and inhabitants of Yerushalayim, lest My wrath come forth like fire and burn, with none to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.”
4.5: Declare in Yahuḏah and let it be heard in Yerushalayim, and say, “Blow the ram’s horn in the land. Cry aloud and say, ‘Gather yourselves, and let us go into the walled city.’
4.6: “Lift up the banner toward Tsiyon. Be strong, do not stand still! For I am bringing evil from the north, and great destruction.”
4.7: “A lion has come up from his bush, and the destroyer of nations is on his way. He has departed from his place to make your land a ruin. Your cities are laid waste, without inhabitant.
4.8: “For this, gird yourself with sackcloth, lament and wail. For the burning displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not turned back from us.
4.9: “And in that day it shall be,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that the heart of the meleḵ shall perish, and the heart of the heads. And the kohenim shall be astonished, and the neḇi’im wonder.”
4.10: Then I said, “Ah, Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! Truly, You have greatly deceived this people and Yerushalayim, saying, ‘Peace is for you,’ whereas the sword reaches to the heart.”
4.11: At that time it shall be said to this people and to Yerushalayim, “A scorching wind of the bare heights blows in the wilderness toward the daughter of My people, not to fan or to cleanse.
4.12: “A wind too strong for this shall come for Me. Now it is I who speak judgments against them.
4.13: “See, he comes up like clouds, and his chariots like a whirlwind. His horses shall be swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we shall be ravaged!”
4.14: O Yerushalayim, wash your heart from evil, and be saved. Till when would your wicked thoughts remain within you?
4.15: For a voice is declaring from Dan, and is proclaiming trouble from Mount Ephrayim:
4.16: “Announce to the nations, look, proclaim against Yerushalayim, that besiegers are coming from a distant land and raise their voice against the cities of Yahuḏah.
4.17: “Like keepers of a field they are against her all around, because she has rebelled against Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
4.18: “Your ways and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your evil, because it is bitter, because it has reached into your heart.”
4.19: O my inward parts, my inward parts! I am in pain! O the walls of my heart! My heart pounds in me, I am not silent. For you have heard, O my being, the sound of the ram’s horn, a shout of battle!
4.20: Destruction upon destruction is cried, for all the land is ravaged. Suddenly my tents are ravaged - my curtains in a moment.
4.21: How long shall I see a banner, and hear the sound of the ram’s horn?
4.22: “For My people are foolish, they have not known Me. They are stupid children, and they have no understanding. They are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge.”
4.23: I looked at the earth, and saw it was formless and empty. And the shamayim, they had no light.
4.24: I looked at the mountains, and saw they shook, and all the hills were swaying.
4.25: I looked, and saw there was no man, and all the birds of the shamayim had fled.
4.26: I looked, and saw the garden land was a wilderness, and all its cities were broken down at the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, by His burning displeasure.
4.27: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “All the earth shall be a ruin, but I shall not make a complete end.
4.28: “On account of this, let the earth mourn and the shamayim above be dark, because I have spoken, because I have purposed and shall not relent, nor do I turn back from it.”
4.29: All the city is fleeing from the noise of the horsemen and bow archers. They shall go into bushes and climb up on the rocks. All the city is forsaken, and no one is dwelling in it.
4.30: And when you are ravaged, what would you do? Though you put on crimson, though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, you adorn yourself in vain. Your lovers despise you, they seek your life.
4.31: For I have heard a voice as of a woman in labor, the distress as of her who brings forth her first child, the voice of the daughter of Tsiyon! She bewails herself, she spreads out her hands, saying, “Woe to me, for my being faints because of murderers!”

40.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 after Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him bound in chains among all the exiles from Yerushalayim and Yahuḏah, who were being exiled to Baḇel.
40.2: And the chief of the guard took Yirmeyahu and said to him, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has spoken this evil on this place.
40.3: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has brought it on, and has done, as He has said. Because you have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and did not obey His voice, therefore this matter has come upon you.
40.4: “And now, see, I loosen you today from the chains that were on your hand. If it seems good to you to come with me to Baḇel, come, and I shall look after you. But if it seems wrong for you to come with me to Baḇel, remain here. See, all the land is before you, go wherever it seems good and right for you to go.”
40.5: And before he replied, “Or go back to Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, whom the meleḵ of Baḇel has made governor over the cities of Yahuḏah, and dwell with him among the people, or go wherever it seems right for you to go.” And the chief of the guard gave him provisions and a gift and let him go.
40.6: So Yirmeyahu went to Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, to Mitspah, and dwelt with him among the people who were left in the land.
40.7: And all the commanders of the armies who were in the fields, they and their men, heard that the meleḵ of Baḇel had made Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam governor in the land, and had put him in charge of the men, and women, and children, and the poor of the land who had not been exiled to Baḇel.
40.8: So they came to Geḏalyahu at Mitspah - Yishma’ĕl the son of Nethanyahu, and Yoḥanan and Yahonathan the sons of Qarĕaḥ, and Serayah the son of Tanḥumeth, and the sons of Ophai the Netophathite and Yezanyahu the son of a Ma’aḵathite, they and their men.
40.9: And Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and their men, saying, “Do not be afraid of serving the Kasdites. Dwell in the land and serve the meleḵ of Baḇel, and it shall be well with you.
40.10: “And I, see, I am dwelling at Mitspah, to serve the Kasdites who come to us. But you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities which you have taken.”
40.11: Also, when all the Yahuḏim who were in Mo’aḇ, and among the Ammonites, and in Eḏom, and who were in all the lands, heard that the meleḵ of Baḇel had left a remnant of Yahuḏah, and that he had appointed over them Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan,
40.12: then all the Yahuḏim returned from all the places where they had been driven, and came to the land of Yahuḏah, to Geḏalyahu at Mitspah, and gathered wine and summer fruit in large quantities.
40.13: And Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ and all the commanders of the army that were in the fields came to Geḏalyahu at Mitspah,
40.14: and they said to him, “Do you know that Ba’alis meleḵ of the Ammonites has sent Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah to take your life?” But Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam would not believe them.
40.15: Then Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ spoke secretly to Geḏalyahu in Mitspah, saying, “Please let me go and smite Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah, without anyone knowing it. Why should he murder you, and so let all the Yahuḏim who are gathered to you be scattered, and the remnant in Yahuḏah perish?”
40.16: But Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam said to Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, “Do not do this matter, for what you are saying about Yishma’ĕl is not true.”

41.1: And in the seventh month it came to be that Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah, son of Elishama, of the royal seed, and of the officers of the meleḵ, came with ten men to Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, at Mitspah. And while they ate bread together there in Mitspah,
41.2: Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah, and the ten men who were with him, arose and smote Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, and killed him whom the meleḵ of Baḇel had made governor over the land.
41.3: And Yishma’ĕl smote all the Yahuḏim who were with him, with Geḏalyahu at Mitspah, and the Kasdites who were found there, the men of battle.
41.4: And it came to be, on the second day after he had killed Geḏalyahu, when no one yet knew it,
41.5: that men came from Sheḵem, from Shiloh, and from Shomeron, eighty men with their beards shaved and their garments torn, having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
41.6: And Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah went out from Mitspah to meet them, weeping as he walked along. And it came to be, as he met them, that he said to them, “Come to Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam!”
41.7: And it came to be, when they came inside the city, that Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah slew them into a pit, he and the men who were with him.
41.8: But ten men were found among them who said to Yishma’ĕl, “Do not kill us, for we have wheat, and barley, and oil, and honey hidden in the field.” So he held back and did not kill them among their brothers.
41.9: And the pit into which Yishma’ĕl had thrown all the corpses of the men whom he had slain, because of Geḏalyahu, was the same one Asa the meleḵ had made for fear of Ba’asha meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl - Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyahu had filled it with the slain.
41.10: Then Yishma’ĕl took captive all the rest of the people who were in Mitspah, the meleḵ’s daughters and all the people who were left in Mitspah, whom Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, had entrusted to Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam. And Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyahu took them captive and went to go over to the Ammonites.
41.11: But Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ and all the commanders of the army that were with him heard of all the evil that Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah had done,
41.12: so they took all the men and went to fight with Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah. And they found him by the great pool that is in Giḇ’on.
41.13: And it came to be, when all the people who were with Yishma’ĕl saw Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, and all the commanders of the army who were with him, that they were glad.
41.14: And all the people whom Yishma’ĕl had taken captive from Mitspah turned around, and came back, and went to Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ.
41.15: But Yishma’ĕl the son of Nethanyah escaped from Yoḥanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.
41.16: Then Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, and all the commanders of the army that were with him, took from Mitspah all the rest of the people whom he had recovered from Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah after he had murdered Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam - the mighty men of battle and the women and the children and the eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Giḇ’on.
41.17: And they departed and dwelt in the lodging place of Kimham, which is near Bĕyth Leḥem, to go to enter Mitsrayim,
41.18: because of the Kasdites. For they were afraid of them, because Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah had smitten Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, whom the meleḵ of Baḇel had made governor in the land.

42.1: Then all the commanders of the army, and Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, and Yezanyah son of Hoshayah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, came near
42.2: and said to Yirmeyahu the naḇi, “We beg you, let our petition be acceptable to you, and pray for us to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, for all this remnant, for we are few left of many, as your eyes see us.
42.3: “And let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim show us the way in which we should walk and the word we should do.”
42.4: And Yirmeyahu the naḇi said to them, “I have heard. See, I am praying to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim according to your words, and it shall be that I declare to you all the word 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answers you. I withhold not a word from you.”
42.5: And they said to Yirmeyahu, “Let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be a true and steadfast witness between us, if we do not do according to all the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim sends us by you.
42.6: “Whether good or evil, let us obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim to whom we send you, in order that it might be well with us when we obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.”
42.7: And after ten days it came to be that the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu.
42.8: So he called Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, and all the commanders of the army which were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
42.9: and said to them, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, to whom you sent me to present your petition before Him,
42.10: ‘If you would indeed stay in this land, then I shall build you and not pull you down, and I shall plant you and not pluck you up. For I have relented of the evil I have done to you.
42.11: ‘Do not be afraid of the meleḵ of Baḇel, of whom you are afraid. Do not be afraid of him,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘for I am with you, to save you and deliver you from his hand.
42.12: ‘And I shall show you compassion, so that he has compassion on you and let you return to your own land.’
42.13: “But if you say, ‘We are not staying in this land,’ and so disobey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
42.14: saying, ‘No, but we are going to the land of Mitsrayim so that we see no fighting, nor hear the sound of the ram’s horn, nor hunger for bread, and there we shall stay,’
42.15: then hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O remnant of Yahuḏah! Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘If you indeed turn your faces to enter Mitsrayim, and shall go to sojourn there,
42.16: then it shall be that the sword which you feared overtakes you there in the land of Mitsrayim, and the scarcity of food of which you were afraid clings to you there in Mitsrayim, and you die there.
42.17: ‘And so it shall be with all the men who turned their faces to go to Mitsrayim to sojourn there: they shall die by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence, and not one of them shall survive or escape from the evil I am bringing upon them.’
42.18: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘As My displeasure and My wrath have been poured out on the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so shall My wrath be poured out on you when you enter Mitsrayim. And you shall be an oath, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach, and you shall see this place no more.’
42.19: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken about you, O remnant of Yahuḏah, ‘Do not go to Mitsrayim!’ Know for certain that I have warned you this day.
42.20: “For you deceived yourselves when you sent me to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, saying, ‘Pray for us to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, and according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim says, so declare to us and we shall do it.’
42.21: “So I have declared it to you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in all which He has sent me to you.
42.22: “And now, know for certain that you shall die by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence in the place where you have desired to go to sojourn.”

43.1: And it came to be, when Yirmeyahu had ended speaking all these words to all the people - all the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, for which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim had sent him to them -
43.2: that Azaryahu son of Hoshayah, and Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, and all the proud men spoke, saying to Yirmeyahu, “You are speaking a lie! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim has not sent you to say, ‘Do not go to Mitsrayim to sojourn there.’
43.3: “For Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah is moving you against us, to give us into the hand of the Kasdites, to put us to death or exile us to Baḇel.”
43.4: So Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, and all the commanders of the army, and all the people disobeyed the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to stay in the land of Yahuḏah.
43.5: And Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ and all the commanders of the army took all the remnant of Yahuḏah who had returned to dwell in the land of Yahuḏah, from all nations where they had been driven -
43.6: the men, and the women, and the children, and the meleḵ’s daughters, and every being whom Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, had left with Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, and Yirmeyahu the naḇi, and Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah.
43.7: So they went to the land of Mitsrayim, for they disobeyed the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they went as far as Taḥpanḥes.
43.8: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Yirmeyahu in Taḥpanḥes, saying,
43.9: “Take large stones in your hand, and you shall hide them before the eyes of the men of Yahuḏah, in the clay in the brick courtyard which is at the entrance to Pharaoh’s house in Taḥpanḥes.
43.10: “Then you shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “See, I am sending, and I shall bring Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel, My servant. And I shall place his throne above these stones that I have hidden. And he shall spread his canopy over them.
43.11: “And he shall come and smite the land of Mitsrayim. Death to those for death, and captivity to those for captivity, and the sword to those for the sword.
43.12: “And he shall light fire to the houses of the mighty ones of Mitsrayim. And he shall burn them and take them captive. And he shall cover himself with the land of Mitsrayim, as a shepherd puts on his garment, and he shall go out from there in peace.
43.13: “And he shall break the stone pillars of Bĕyth Shemesh which are in the land of Mitsrayim, and he shall burn the houses of the mighty ones of the Mitsrites with fire.” ’ ”

44.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu concerning all the Yahuḏim who were dwelling in the land of Mitsrayim - who were dwelling at Miḡdol, and at Taḥpanḥes, and at Noph, and in the land of Pathros, saying,
44.2: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘You yourselves have seen all the evil that I have brought on Yerushalayim and on all the cities of Yahuḏah. And see, this day they are a ruin, and no one dwells in them,
44.3: because of their evil which they have done to provoke Me, by going to burn incense by serving other mighty ones whom they did not know, they nor you nor your fathers.
44.4: ‘And I sent to you all My servants the neḇi’im, rising early and sending them, saying, “Please do not do this abominable matter that I hate!”
44.5: ‘But they did not listen or incline their ear, to turn from their evil, not to burn incense to other mighty ones.
44.6: ‘So My wrath and My displeasure were poured out and burned in the cities of Yahuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, and they became a ruin and a wasteland, as it is this day.’
44.7: “And now, thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Why are you doing this great evil against your lives, to cut off from you man and woman, child and infant, from the midst of Yahuḏah, leaving none to remain,
44.8: by provoking Me with the works of your hands, by burning incense to other mighty ones in the land of Mitsrayim where you have gone to dwell, to cut yourselves off and be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
44.9: ‘Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, and the evils of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah, and the evils of their wives, and your own evils, and the evils of your wives, which they have done in the land of Yahuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim?
44.10: ‘To this day they have not been humbled, nor have they revered, nor have they walked in My Torah and in My Laws that I put before you and your fathers.’
44.11: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘See, I am turning My face against you for evil and for cutting off all Yahuḏah.
44.12: ‘And I shall take the remnant of Yahuḏah who have turned their faces to go into the land of Mitsrayim to sojourn there. And they shall all be consumed in the land of Mitsrayim - fall by the sword, consumed by scarcity of food. From the least to the greatest they shall die, by the sword and by scarcity of food. And they shall be a cursing and an astonishment and a curse and a reproach!
44.13: ‘And I shall punish those dwelling in the land of Mitsrayim, as I have punished Yerushalayim, by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence.
44.14: ‘And none of the remnant of Yahuḏah who have gone into the land of Mitsrayim to sojourn there shall escape or survive, lest they return to the land of Yahuḏah, to which they are longing to return to dwell there. For they shall not return, except those who escape.’ ”
44.15: Then all the men who knew that their wives had burned incense to other mighty ones, and all the women who stood by, a great assembly, and all the people who dwelt in the land of Mitsrayim, in Pathros, answered Yirmeyahu, saying,
44.16: “We are not going to listen to you in the matter about which you spoke to us in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
44.17: “But we shall do whatever has gone out of our own mouth, to burn incense to the queen of the shamayim and pour out drink offerings to her, as we have done, we and our fathers, our melaḵim and our heads, in the cities of Yahuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim. And we had plenty of food, and were well-off, and saw no evil.
44.18: “But since we ceased burning incense to the queen of the shamayim and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked all and have been consumed by the sword and by scarcity of food.
44.19: “And when we burned incense to the queen of the shamayim and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her, to idolize her, and pour out drink offerings to her, without our husbands?”
44.20: Then Yirmeyahu spoke to all the people - to the men and to the women, and to all the people who had given him that answer, saying,
44.21: “As for the incense that you burned in the cities of Yahuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, you and your fathers, your melaḵim and your heads, and the people of the land, did not 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 remember them? And it came into His heart!
44.22: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 could no longer bear it, because of the evil of your deeds and because of the abominations which you did. Therefore your land is a ruin, an object of astonishment, a curse, and without an inhabitant, as it is this day.
44.23: “Because you have burned incense and because you have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 or walk in His Torah, in His Laws or in His Witnesses, therefore this evil has befallen you, as at this day.”
44.24: And Yirmeyahu said to all the people and to all the women, “Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all Yahuḏah who are in the land of Mitsrayim!
44.25: “Thus spoke 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘You and your wives have spoken with your mouths, and have filled with your hands, saying, “We shall perform our vows that we have made, to burn incense to the queen of the shamayim and pour out drink offerings to her.” Then confirm your vows and perform your vows!’
44.26: “Therefore hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all Yahuḏah who are dwelling in the land of Mitsrayim, ‘See, I have sworn by My great Name,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘My Name shall no longer be called upon by the mouth of any man of Yahuḏah in all the land of Mitsrayim, saying, “As Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives…”
44.27: ‘See, I am watching over them for evil and not for good. And all the men of Yahuḏah who are in the land of Mitsrayim shall be consumed by the sword and by scarcity of food, until they come to an end.
