44.28: ‘And those who escape the sword, few in number, shall return from the land of Mitsrayim to the land of Yahuḏah. And all the remnant of Yahuḏah, who came into the land of Mitsrayim to sojourn there, shall know whose word is established, Mine or theirs.
44.29: ‘And this is the sign to you,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘that I am punishing you in this place, so that you know that My words are certainly established against you for evil.’
44.30: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I am giving Pharaoh Ḥophra meleḵ of Mitsrayim into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, as I gave Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, his enemy who sought his life.’ ”

45.1: The word that Yirmeyahu the naḇi spoke to Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah, when he had written these words in a book from the mouth of Yirmeyahu, in the fourth year of Yahoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, saying,
45.2: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, concerning you, Baruḵ:
45.3: ‘You have said, “Woe to me now! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has added grief to my pain. I have been wearied with my sighing, and I have found no rest.” ’
45.4: “Say this to him, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, what I have built I am breaking down, and what I have planted I am plucking up, that is, the entire land.
45.5: “And do you seek great matters for yourself? Do not seek them, for look, I am bringing evil on all flesh,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “But I shall give your life to you as a prize in all places, wherever you go.” ’ ”

46.1: The word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which came to Yirmeyahu the naḇi concerning the gentiles:
46.2: For Mitsrayim, concerning the army of Pharaoh Neḵo, meleḵ of Mitsrayim, which was by the River Perath in Karkemish, and which Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel had smitten in the fourth year of Yahoyaqim, son of Yoshiyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah:
46.3: “Prepare the large and the small shield, and draw near to battle!
46.4: “Harness the horses, and mount up, you horsemen! Stand with helmets, polish the spears, put on the armor!
46.5: “Why do I see them afraid, turned back? And their fighters are beaten down. And they have fled in haste, and did not look back, for fear was all around,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
46.6: Do not let the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape. They shall stumble and fall toward the north, by the River Perath.
46.7: Who is this rising like a flood, whose waters surge about like the rivers?
46.8: Mitsrayim rises like a flood, and its waters surge about like the rivers. And he says, ‘Let me rise and cover the earth; let me destroy the city and its inhabitants.’
46.9: Go up, O horses, and rage, O chariots! And let the mighty men go forth - Kush and Put who handle the shield, and Luḏ who handle and bend the bow.
46.10: For this is the day of Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, a day of vengeance, to revenge Himself on His adversaries. And the sword shall devour, and be satisfied and made drunk with their blood. For Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts has a slaughtering in the land of the north by the River Perath.
46.11: Go up to Gil’aḏ and take balm, O maiden, the daughter of Mitsrayim. In vain you have used many remedies, there is no healing for you.
46.12: Nations have heard of your shame, and your cry has filled the land. For the mighty has stumbled against the mighty, they have both fallen together.
46.13: The word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Yirmeyahu the naḇi, about the coming of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, to smite the land of Mitsrayim:
46.14: “Declare in Mitsrayim, and let it be heard in Miḡdol. And let it be heard in Noph and in Taḥpanḥes. Say, ‘Stand fast and be prepared, for a sword shall devour all around you.’
46.15: “Why were your strong ones swept away? They did not stand because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 drove them away.
46.16: “He made many stumble; indeed, they fell over each other, and said, ‘Arise! Let us go back to our own people, and to the land of our birth, away from the oppressing sword.’
46.17: “There they cried, ‘Pharaoh, meleḵ of Mitsrayim, is but a noise. He has let the appointed time pass by!’
46.18: “As I live,” declares the Meleḵ, whose Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “For as Taḇor is among the mountains, and as Karmel by the sea, he shall come.
46.19: “O you daughter dwelling in Mitsrayim, prepare yourself to go into exile! For Noph shall become a waste and a ruin, and be burned, without inhabitant.
46.20: “Mitsrayim is like a very pretty heifer, but destruction comes, it comes from the north.
46.21: “Her hired ones too, in her midst, are like fattened calves, for they too shall turn, they shall flee away together. They shall not stand, for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
46.22: “Its sound moves along like a serpent, for they move on like an army and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.
46.23: “They shall cut down her forest,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “for it is not searched, because they are more numerous than locusts, and without number.
46.24: “The daughter of Mitsrayim shall be put to shame. She shall be given into the hand of the people of the north.”
46.25: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, has said, “See, I am bringing punishment on Amon of No, and on Pharaoh, and on Mitsrayim, and on their mighty ones, and on their melaḵim, and on Pharaoh and on those trusting in him.
46.26: “And I shall give them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel and into the hand of his servants. And afterward it shall be inhabited as in the days of old,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
46.27: “But as for you, do not fear, O My servant Ya’aqoḇ, and do not be discouraged, O Yisra’ĕl! For look, I am saving you from afar, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. And Ya’aqoḇ shall return, and shall have rest and be at ease, with no one disturbing.
46.28: “Do not fear, O Ya’aqoḇ My servant,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “for I am with you. Though I make a complete end of all the gentiles to which I have driven you, yet I do not make a complete end of you. But I shall reprove you in right-ruling, and by no means leave you unpunished.”

47.1: The word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that came to Yirmeyahu the naḇi concerning the Pelishtites, before Pharaoh smote Azzah:
47.2: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, waters are rising out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood. And they shall overflow the land and all that is in it, the city and those who dwell within. And men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail.
47.3: “At the noise of the stamping hooves of his strong horses, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look to their children, because of weakness of hands,
47.4: because of the day that shall come to ravage all the Pelishtites, to cut off from Tsor and Tsiḏon every helper that survives. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is ravaging the Pelishtites, the remnant of the isle of Kaphtor.
47.5: “Baldness shall come upon Azzah, Ashqelon shall be cut off with the remnant of their valley. Till when would you cut yourself?
47.6: “O you sword of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, how long till you rest? Put yourself up into your sheath, rest and be still!
47.7: “How shall it rest, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given it a command? Against Ashqelon and against the seashore - there He has appointed it.”

48.1: Concerning Mo’aḇ. This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl said, “Woe to Neḇo! For it is ravaged, Qiryathayim is put to shame, captured. The high stronghold is put to shame and broken down.
48.2: “There is praise for Mo’aḇ no longer. In Ḥeshbon they have devised evil against her, ‘Come and let us cut it off as a nation.’ O Maḏmĕn, you are also cut off, a sword goes after you.
48.3: “Listen! An outcry from Ḥoronayim, ravaging and great destruction!
48.4: “Mo’aḇ shall be destroyed, her little ones shall cry out.
48.5: “For on the ascent to Luḥith they go up weeping bitterly. For in the descent of Ḥoronayim the enemies shall hear a cry of destruction.
48.6: “Flee, deliver your own lives! And be like a bush in the wilderness.
48.7: “For because you have trusted in your works and your treasures, you shall be captured. And Kemosh shall go forth into exile, his priests and his heads together.
48.8: “And a ravager shall come into every city, no one escapes. And the valley shall perish, and the plain be destroyed, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken.
48.9: “Give wings to Mo’aḇ, for she has to flee away, and her cities become a ruin, with no one to dwell in them.
48.10: “Cursed is he who is slack in doing the work of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and cursed is he who withholds his sword from blood.
48.11: “Mo’aḇ has been at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his dregs, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. Therefore his flavor has stayed in him, and his fragrance is unchanged.
48.12: “Therefore see, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when I shall send him tilters, who shall tilt him over and empty his vessels and break the pitchers.
48.13: “And Mo’aḇ shall be ashamed because of Kemosh, as the house of Yisra’ĕl was ashamed of Bĕyth Ĕl, their refuge.
48.14: “How do you say, ‘We are mighty and strong men for battle’?
48.15: “Mo’aḇ is ravaged and her cities have been entered. And her chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter,” declares the Meleḵ, whose Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts.
48.16: “The calamity of Mo’aḇ is near to come and his affliction hurries fast.
48.17: “Lament for him, all you who are around him. And all you who know his name, say, ‘How the strong sceptre has been broken, the staff of splendor!’
48.18: “Come down from your esteem, and sit in thirst, O inhabitant, daughter of Diḇon. For the ravager of Mo’aḇ shall come against you, he shall destroy your strongholds.
48.19: “Stand by the way and watch, O inhabitant of Aro’ĕr. Ask him who flees and her who escapes; say, ‘What has been done?’
48.20: “Mo’aḇ has been put to shame, for it has been broken down. Howl and cry! Let it be heard in Arnon that Mo’aḇ is ravaged.
48.21: “And judgment has come on the plain country, on Ḥolon and on Yahtsah and on Mopha’ath,
48.22: and on Diḇon and Neḇo and on Bĕyth Diḇlathayim,
48.23: and on Qiryathayim and on Bĕyth Gamul and on Bĕyth Me’on,
48.24: and on Qeriyoth and on Botsrah and on all the cities of the land of Mo’aḇ, far and near.
48.25: “The horn of Mo’aḇ has been cut off, and his arm has been broken,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
48.26: “Make him drunk, because he has made himself great against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Mo’aḇ shall splash in his vomit, and he shall also be in mockery.
48.27: “And was not Yisra’ĕl a mockery to you? Was he found among thieves? For whenever you speak of him, you shake your head.
48.28: “O inhabitants of Mo’aḇ, leave the cities and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove making a nest in the sides of the cave’s mouth.
48.29: “We have heard of the pride of Mo’aḇ. He is very proud of his loftiness and arrogance and pride, and of the haughtiness of his heart.”
48.30: “I know his wrath,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and his boastings are untrue. His deeds are false.
48.31: “Therefore I wail for Mo’aḇ, and I cry out for all Mo’aḇ. I mourn for the men of Qir Ḥeres.
48.32: “O vine of Siḇmah! I weep for you with the weeping of Ya’zĕr. Your branches have passed over the sea, they have come to the sea of Ya’zĕr. The ravager has fallen on your summer fruit and your grape harvest.
48.33: “Joy and gladness have been taken away from the orchard and from the land of Mo’aḇ. And I have made wine to cease from the winepresses. No one treads with shouting - the shouting is no shouting!
48.34: “From the outcry of Ḥeshbon unto El’alĕh, unto Yahats, they shall raise their voice, from Tso’ar to Ḥoronayim, like a three-year-old heifer, for even the waters of Nimrim are dried up.
48.35: “And I shall make an end in Mo’aḇ to him who offers in the high places and burns incense to his mighty ones,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
48.36: “So My heart sounds for Mo’aḇ like flutes, and My heart sounds for the men of Qir Ḥeres like flutes. Therefore the wealth they made shall be gone.
48.37: “For every head is bald, and every beard clipped - cuts on all the hands, and sackcloth on the loins.
48.38: “On all the house-tops of Mo’aḇ and in its streets it is all lamentation, for I have broken Mo’aḇ like a vessel in which no one delights,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
48.39: “How she has been broken down! They shall wail! How Mo’aḇ has turned her back with shame! So Mo’aḇ shall be a mockery and a horror to all those about her.”
48.40: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, he soars like an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Mo’aḇ.
48.41: “Qeriyoth shall be captured, and the strongholds seized. And the heart of the mighty men in Mo’aḇ on that day shall be like the heart of a woman in labor.
48.42: “And Mo’aḇ shall be destroyed as a people, because he has made himself great against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
48.43: “Fear and the pit and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of Mo’aḇ,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
48.44: “He who flees from the fear falls into the pit, and he who gets out of the pit is caught in the snare. For I am bringing upon Mo’aḇ the year of their punishment,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
48.45: “Those who fled stood powerless under the shadow of Ḥeshbon. But a fire shall come out of Ḥeshbon, and a flame from the midst of Siḥon, and consume the brow of Mo’aḇ and the crown of the head of the sons of Sha’on.
48.46: “Woe to you, O Mo’aḇ! The people of Kemosh have perished, for your sons have been taken into exile, and your daughters into exile.
48.47: “But I shall turn back the captivity of Mo’aḇ in the latter days,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Thus far is the judgment of Mo’aḇ.

49.1: Concerning the Ammonites: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Has Yisra’ĕl no sons? Has he no heir? Why has Malkam taken possession of Gaḏ, and his people dwell in its cities?
49.2: “Therefore see, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when I shall sound a battle cry in Rabbah of the Ammonites. And it shall be a heap, a wasteland, and her villages shall be burned with fire. Then Yisra’ĕl shall dispossess those who dispossessed him,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
49.3: “Howl, O Ḥeshbon, for Ai is ravaged! Cry, daughters of Rabbah, gird on sackcloth! Lament and diligently search by the walls, for Malkam shall go into exile, with his priests and his heads.
49.4: “Why do you boast in the valleys, your flowing valley, O backsliding daughter who is trusting in her treasures, saying, ‘Who would come against me?’
49.5: “See, I am bringing fear upon you, from all those around you,” declares Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts. “And you shall be driven out, each one straight ahead, with no one to bring home the wanderer.
49.6: “And after this I turn back the captivity of the children of Ammon,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
49.7: Concerning Eḏom: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “Is there no more wisdom in Tĕman? Has counsel been lost to those with understanding? Has their wisdom vanished?
49.8: “Flee, turn back, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Deḏan! For I shall bring the calamity of Ĕsaw upon him, the time that I shall punish him.
49.9: “If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? Even thieves by night would destroy until they had enough!
49.10: “But as for Me, I shall make Ĕsaw bare. I shall uncover his hiding places, so that he is unable to conceal himself. His seed is ravaged, his brothers and his neighbors, and he is no more.
49.11: “Leave your fatherless children, let Me keep them alive. And let your widows trust in Me.”
49.12: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, those whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have certainly drunk. And are you the one to go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, but certainly drink of it.
49.13: “For I have sworn by Myself,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that Botsrah is to become a ruin, a reproach, a waste, and a curse, and all its cities become everlasting wastes.”
49.14: I have heard a report from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and an envoy has been sent to the nations, “Gather together, come against her, and rise up to battle!
49.15: “For look, I shall make you small among nations, despised among men.
49.16: “The dread for you, the pride of your heart, has deceived you, O you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, holding the height of the hill! Though you make your nest as high as the eagle, from there I bring you down,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
49.17: “And Eḏom shall be a ruin, everyone who passes by it is astonished and whistles at all its plagues.
49.18: “As in the overthrow of Seḏom and Amorah and their neighboring cities,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “No one shall dwell there, nor would a son of man sojourn in it.
49.19: “See, he comes up like a lion from the pride of the Yardĕn against the home of the strong. But in an instant I shall make him run away from her. And who is the Chosen One to appoint over her? For who is like Me? And who summons Me? And who is that Shepherd who stands before Me?”
49.20: Therefore hear the counsel of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He has counselled concerning Eḏom, and the purposes He has purposed concerning the inhabitants of Tĕman: the least of the flock shall drag them away! He shall make their pasture a waste before them!
49.21: The earth shall be shaken at the noise of their fall. There is an outcry! Its noise is heard at the Sea of Reeds.
49.22: See, like an eagle he flies up, and spreads his wings over Botsrah. And the heart of the mighty men of Eḏom in that day shall be like the heart of a woman in her pain.
49.23: Concerning Dammeseq: “Ḥamath and Arpaḏ have been put to shame, for they have heard an evil report. They have been melted in anxiety, like the sea, unable to rest.
49.24: “Dammeseq has become feeble, she has turned to flee, and trembling has seized her. Distress and pain have taken hold of her like a woman in labor.
49.25: “How is the city of praise deserted, the city of My joy!
49.26: “Therefore her young men fall in her streets, and all the men of battle are cut off in that day,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts.
49.27: “And I shall kindle a fire in the wall of Dammeseq, and it shall consume the palaces of Ben-Haḏaḏ.”
49.28: To Qĕḏar and to the reigns of Ḥatsor, which Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel smote: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Arise, go up to Qĕḏar, and ravage the men of the East!
49.29: “Their tents and their flocks, their curtains and all their vessels shall be taken. And they shall take away their camels for themselves. And they shall cry out to them, ‘Fear is on every side!’
49.30: “Flee, go away! Dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Ḥatsor!” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “For Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel has taken counsel against you, and has devised a plan against you.
49.31: “Arise, go up to the nation at ease that dwells safely,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “It has no gates or bars, they dwell alone.
49.32: “And their camels shall become plunder, and their large herds booty. And I shall scatter them to all winds, those who cut off the corner, and bring their calamity from all its sides,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
49.33: “Ḥatsor shall be a habitation for jackals, a desert forever. No one dwells there, nor does son of man sojourn in it.”
49.34: The word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that came to Yirmeyahu the naḇi concerning Ĕylam, in the beginning of the reign of Tsiḏqiyahu, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, saying,
49.35: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, ‘See, I am breaking the bow of Ĕylam, the chief of their might.
49.36: ‘And I shall bring upon Ĕylam the four winds from the four quarters of the shamayim, and scatter them toward all those winds. And there shall be no nation where the outcasts of Ĕylam do not go.
49.37: ‘And I shall break Ĕylam before their enemies and before those who seek their life. And I shall bring evil upon them, my burning displeasure,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. ‘And I shall send the sword after them until I have consumed them.
49.38: ‘And I shall place My throne in Ĕylam, and destroy from there the meleḵ and the heads,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
49.39: ‘And it shall be in the latter days that turn back the captivity of Ĕylam,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

5.1: “Diligently search the streets of Yerushalayim, and please look, and know and seek in her open places if you find a man, if there is anyone doing Right-Ruling, seeking the truth, then I shall pardon her.
5.2: “Even when they say, ‘As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives,’ they swear falsely, for certain.”
5.3: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are Your eyes, not on truth? You have smitten them, but they have not grieved. You have consumed them, but they have refused to receive instruction. They made their faces harder than rock, they refused to turn back.
5.4: Then I said, “These are only the poor. They have been foolish, for they have not known the Way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Right-Ruling of their Elohim.
5.5: “Let me go to the great men and speak to them, for they have known the Way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Right-Ruling of their Elohim.” But these have altogether broken the yoke and torn off the bonds.
5.6: Therefore a lion from the forest shall smite them, a wolf of the deserts ravage them. A leopard is watching over their cities, whoever comes out of them is torn in pieces. For their transgressions have been many, their backslidings have been numerous.
5.7: “Why should I pardon you for this? Your children have forsaken Me and sworn by those that are not mighty ones. When I had filled them up, they then committed adultery and they thronged to the house of a whore.
5.8: “They were like well-fed horses, each one neighed after his neighbor’s wife.
5.9: “Would I not punish them for this?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “And would I not revenge Myself on such a nation as this?
5.10: “Go up on her walls and destroy, but do not make a complete end. Take away her branches, for they do not belong to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
5.11: “For the house of Yisra’ĕl and the house of Yahuḏah have utterly betrayed Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
5.12: They have been untrue to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and said, “It is not He. No evil comes upon us, nor do we see sword or scarcity of food.”
5.13: And the neḇi’im have become wind, and the Word is not in them. Thus shall be done to them:
5.14: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of hosts, “Because you speak this word, see, I am making My words in your mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.
5.15: “See, I am bringing a nation against you from afar, O house of Yisra’ĕl,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “It is an enduring nation, it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know, nor do you understand what they say.
5.16: “Their quiver is like an open tomb, all of them are mighty men.
5.17: “And they shall eat up your harvest and your bread, which your sons and daughters should eat. They shall eat up your flocks and your herds, they shall eat up your vines and your fig trees. With the sword they shall demolish your walled cities, in which you are trusting.
5.18: “But even in those days,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I shall not make a complete end of you.
5.19: “And it shall be, when they say, ‘Why does 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim do all this to us?’ then you shall answer them, ‘As you have forsaken Me and served foreign mighty ones in your land, so you shall serve foreigners in a land that is not yours.’
5.20: “Declare this in the house of Ya’aqoḇ and proclaim it in Yahuḏah, saying,
5.21: ‘Hear this now, O foolish people without heart, who have eyes and see not, and who have ears and hear not:
5.22: ‘Do you not revere Me?’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. ‘Do you not tremble at My presence, who have placed the sand as the boundary of the sea, by an everlasting law, and it does not pass over it? Though its waves toss to and fro, they are not able; though they roar, they do not pass over it.
5.23: ‘But this people has a backsliding and rebellious heart, they have turned aside and gone away.
5.24: ‘And they do not say in their heart, “Let us now revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, who gives rain, both the former and the latter, in its season. He guards for us the Law: the Shaḇuoth of harvest.”
5.25: ‘Your wickednesses have turned these away, and your sins have kept the good from you.
5.26: ‘For among My people are found wicked men who lie in wait as one who lays snares. They have laid up a trap, they catch men.
5.27: ‘As a cage is filled with birds, so their houses are filled with deceit. Therefore they have become great and grown rich.
5.28: ‘They have become fat, they are sleek. They also overlook the deeds of the wicked. They did not rightly rule the cause of the fatherless, so that they prosper. And the right of the needy they did not rightly rule.
5.29: ‘Would I not punish them for this?’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. ‘Would I not revenge Myself on such a nation as this?’
5.30: “An astounding and horrible matter has come to be in the land:
5.31: The neḇi’im have naḇu falsely, and the kohenim rule by their own hand, and My people have loved it so. And what are you going to do at the end of it?

50.1: The word that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke concerning Baḇel, concerning the land of the Kasdites by Yirmeyahu the naḇi.
50.2: “Declare among the nations, and let it be heard. And lift up a banner, let it be heard, and do not conceal it. Say, ‘Baḇel shall be taken, Bĕl shall be put to shame, Meroḏaḵ shall be broken, her images shall be put to shame, her idols shall be broken.’
50.3: For a nation shall come up against her from the north, which shall make her land waste, and none shall dwell in it. They shall flee, they shall go, both man and beast.
50.4: “In those days and at that time,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “the children of Yisra’ĕl shall come, they and the children of Yahuḏah together, weeping as they come, and seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim.
50.5: “They shall ask the way to Tsiyon, their faces toward it, ‘Come and let us join ourselves to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in an everlasting Covenant, never to be forgotten.’
50.6: “My people have been wandering sheep. Their shepherds have led them astray, turning them away on the mountains. They have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their resting place.
50.7: “All who found them have devoured them. And their adversaries have said, ‘We are not guilty, because they have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Home of righteousness, and the Expectation of their fathers: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’
50.8: “Flee from the midst of Baḇel, come out of the land of the Kasdites. And be as rams before a flock.
50.9: “For look, I am stirring up and bringing up against Baḇel an assembly of great nations from a land of the north, and they shall array themselves against her. From there she shall be captured - their arrows are like those of a mighty skilled man, not returning empty-handed.
50.10: “And Kasdim shall become plunder, all who plunder her shall satisfy themselves,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
50.11: “Because you were glad, because you rejoiced, you who plunder My inheritance, because you have grown fat like a heifer threshing grain, and you neigh like stallions,
50.12: your mother shall be greatly ashamed. She who bore you shall be humiliated. Look, the last of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land and a desert.
50.13: “Because of the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 she shall not be inhabited, but she shall be deserted - all of it. Everyone passing by Baḇel shall be astonished and whistle at all her plagues.
50.14: “Arrange yourselves against Baḇel all around, all you who bend the bow. Shoot at her, spare no arrows, for she has sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
50.15: “Shout against her all around. She has given her hand, her foundations have fallen, her walls are thrown down, for it is the vengeance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Take vengeance on her. As she has done, so do to her.
50.16: “Cut off the sower from Baḇel, and him who handles the sickle at harvest time. From before the sword of the oppressor each one turns to his own people, and each one flees to his own land.
50.17: “Yisra’ĕl is a scattered sheep, the lions have driven him away. First the meleḵ of Ashshur devoured him, and now, at last, this Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel has broken his bones.”
50.18: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “See, I am punishing the meleḵ of Baḇel and his land, as I have punished the meleḵ of Ashshur.
50.19: “And I shall bring back Yisra’ĕl to his pasture, and he shall feed on Karmel and Bashan. And his being shall be satisfied on Mount Ephrayim and Gil’aḏ.
50.20: “In those days and at that time,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “the wickedness of Yisra’ĕl shall be searched for, but there shall be none; and the sin of Yahuḏah, but none shall be found. For I shall pardon those whom I leave as a remnant.
50.21: “Go up against the land of Merathayim, against it, and against the inhabitants of Peqoḏ. Slay and put them under the ban,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and do according to all that I have commanded you.
50.22: “There is a sound of battle in the land, and of great destruction.
50.23: “How the hammer of all the earth has been cut off and broken! How Baḇel has become a ruin among the nations!
50.24: “I have laid a snare for you, and you were captured, O Baḇel, and you yourself did not know! You have been found and also caught, because you strove against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
50.25: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has opened His armory, and has brought out the weapons of His displeasure, for Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts has a work to do in the land of the Kasdites.
50.26: Come against her from every quarter, open her storehouses, pile her up as heaps of ruins, and put her under the ban. Let her have no remnant.
50.27: Slay all her bulls, let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them! For their day has come, the time of their punishment.
50.28: Listen! They flee and escape from the land of Baḇel, to declare in Tsiyon the vengeance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, the vengeance of His Hĕyḵal.
50.29: “Summon archers against Baḇel. All you who bend the bow, encamp against it all around, let no one escape. Repay her according to her work, do to her according to all she has done. For she has been proud against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, against the Qadosh One of Yisra’ĕl.
50.30: “Therefore her young men shall fall in the streets, and all her men of battle shall perish in that day,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
50.31: “See, I am against you, O proud one!” declares Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “for your day has come, the time for your punishment.
50.32: “And the proud one shall stumble, and he shall fall, with no one to raise him up. And I shall kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all around him.”
50.33: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “The children of Yisra’ĕl were oppressed, along with the children of Yahuḏah. And all who took them captive have held them fast, they refused to let them go.
50.34: “Their Redeemer is strong, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts is His Name. He shall strongly plead their case, so as to give rest to the land, but unrest to the inhabitants of Baḇel.
50.35: “A sword is upon the Kasdites,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and it is upon the inhabitants of Baḇel, and upon her heads and upon her wise men.
50.36: “A sword is upon the liars, and they shall be fools. A sword is upon her mighty men, and they shall be broken down.
50.37: “A sword is upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the mixed peoples who are in her midst, and they shall become like women. A sword is upon her treasures, and they shall be plundered.
50.38: “A sword is upon her waters, and they shall be dried up. For it is a land of carved images, and they boast about their idols.
50.39: “Therefore the wild desert beasts shall dwell with the jackals, and the ostriches dwell in it. And it shall never again be inhabited, nor dwelt in, unto all generations.
50.40: “As Elohim overthrew Seḏom and Amorah and their neighboring cities,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “so no one would dwell there, nor would son of man sojourn in it.
50.41: “See, a people shall come from the north, and a great nation and many melaḵim stirred up from the ends of the earth.
50.42: “They lay hold of bow and spear, they are cruel and they show no compassion. They sound like the roaring sea, and ride on horses, put in array, like a man for the battle, against you, O daughter of Baḇel.
50.43: “The meleḵ of Baḇel has heard the report about them, and his hands became weak. Distress has seized him, pain like that of a woman in labor.
50.44: “See, he comes up like a lion from the pride of the Yardĕn, against the enduring pasture. But in an instant I shall make them run away from her. And who is the Chosen One whom I appoint against her? For who is like Me? Who summons Me? And who is that Shepherd who stands before Me?”
50.45: Therefore hear the counsel of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He has counselled concerning Baḇel, and His purposes He has purposed concerning the land of the Kasdites: the least of the flock shall drag them away! He shall make their pasture a waste before them!
50.46: At the sound of Baḇel’s capture the earth shall be shaken, and the outcry shall be heard among the nations.

51.1: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am stirring up the spirit of a destroyer against Baḇel, against those who dwell in Leḇ - My opponents.
51.2: And I shall send winnowers to Baḇel, who shall winnow her and empty her land. For they shall be against her all around, in the day of evil.
51.3: “Let the archer draw his bow, and let him stand ready in his armor. Do not spare her young men, put all her army under the ban.
51.4: “And the slain shall fall in the land of the Kasdites, and the pierced-through in her streets.
51.5: “For neither Yisra’ĕl nor Yahuḏah is widowed by his Elohim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, though their land has been filled with sin against the Qadosh One of Yisra’ĕl.”
51.6: Flee from the midst of Baḇel and let each one save his life! Do not be cut off in her wickedness, for this is the time of the vengeance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the recompense He is repaying her.
51.7: Baḇel was a golden cup in the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, making drunk all the earth. The nations drank her wine, that is why the nations went mad!
51.8: Baḇel shall suddenly fall and be broken. Howl for her! Take balm for her pain - if so be, she might be healed.
51.9: We would have healed Baḇel, but she is not healed. Let us leave her and each go to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the shamayim and is lifted up to the clouds.
51.10: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has brought forth our righteousness. Come and let us declare in Tsiyon the work of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim.
51.11: Polish the arrows! Put on the shields! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has stirred up the spirit of the melaḵim of the Maḏites. For His plan is against Baḇel to destroy it, because it is the vengeance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the vengeance for His Hĕyḵal.
51.12: Lift up a banner on the walls of Baḇel, strengthen the watch, station the watchmen, prepare the ambush. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has both planned and done what He spoke concerning the inhabitants of Baḇel.
51.13: You who dwell upon many waters, great in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your greedy gain.
51.14: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts has sworn by Himself, “I shall certainly fill you with men, as with locusts, and they shall lift up a shout against you.”
51.15: He made the earth by His power, He established the world by His wisdom, and stretched out the shamayim by His understanding.
51.16: When He gives forth His voice the waters in the shamayim roar, and He makes vapors to ascend from the ends of the earth; He makes lightnings for the rain, and He brings the wind out of His treasuries.
51.17: All mankind has become too brutish to know, every smith has been put to shame by the carved image, for his molded image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
51.18: They are worthless, a work of mockery. In the time of their punishment they perish.
51.19: The Portion of Ya’aqoḇ is not like them, for He is the Maker of all, and Yisra’ĕl is the tribe of His inheritance. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts is His Name.
51.20: “You are My battle-axe, weapons of battle, and with you I shall break nations in pieces, and with you I shall destroy reigns.
51.21: “And with you I shall break in pieces the horse and its rider, and with you I shall break in pieces the chariot and its rider.
51.22: “And with you I shall break in pieces man and woman, and with you I shall break in pieces old and young, and with you I shall break in pieces the young man and the maiden.
51.23: “And with you I shall break in pieces the shepherd and his flock, and with you I shall break in pieces the farmer and his yoke of oxen. And with you I shall break in pieces governors and rulers.
51.24: “And I shall repay Baḇel and all the inhabitants of Kasdim for all the evil they have done in Tsiyon before your eyes,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
51.25: “See, I am against you, O destroying mountain, who destroys all the earth,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “And I shall stretch out My hand against you. And I shall roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burnt mountain.
51.26: “And they shall not take from you a stone for a corner nor a stone for a foundation, but you shall be a waste forever,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
51.27: Lift up a banner in the land, blow the ram’s horn among the nations! Prepare the nations against her, call the reigns together against her: Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her, bring up horses like hairy locusts.
51.28: Separate the nations against her, with the melaḵim of the Maḏites, its governors and all its rulers, all the land of his rule,
51.29: so that the land shakes and writhes in pain. For every plan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be established against Baḇel, to make the land of Baḇel a ruin, without inhabitant.
51.30: The mighty men of Baḇel have ceased to fight, they remained in their strongholds. Their might has failed, they became like women, they have burned her dwelling places. The bars of her gate have been broken.
51.31: One runner runs to meet another, and one reporter to meet another, to report to the meleḵ of Baḇel that his city is taken on all sides,
51.32: and the fords have been captured, and they have burned the reeds with fire, and the soldiers are startled.
51.33: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “The daughter of Baḇel is like a threshing-floor at the time it is trodden. Yet a little while and the time of her harvest shall come.”
51.34: “Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel has devoured us, he has crushed us, he has made us an empty vessel, he has swallowed us up like a dragon. He has filled his stomach with my delicacies, he has driven us away.
51.35: “Let the violence done to me and my flesh be upon Baḇel,” says the inhabitant of Tsiyon. And, “Let my blood be upon the inhabitants of Kasdim,” says Yerushalayim.
51.36: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am pleading your case. And I shall take vengeance for you and dry up her sea and make her fountain dry.
51.37: “And Baḇel shall become a heap, a habitation of jackals, an astonishment and a hissing, without inhabitant.
51.38: “Together they roar like lions, they shall growl like lions’ cubs.
51.39: “In their heat I prepare their feasts. And I shall make them drunk, so that they rejoice, and sleep a never-ending sleep and not awake,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
51.40: “I shall bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
51.41: “Oh, how Shĕshaḵ has been captured, the praise of all the earth been seized! How Baḇel has become a ruin among the nations!
51.42: “The sea has risen over Baḇel, she has been covered with the roaring of its waves.
51.43: “Her cities have become a ruin, a dry land and a desert, a land where no one dwells, neither does a son of man pass by it.
51.44: “And I shall punish Bĕl in Baḇel. And I shall make him spew out what he has swallowed, and nations shall no longer stream to him. Even the wall of Baḇel shall fall.
51.45: “Come out of her midst, My people! And let everyone deliver his being from the burning displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
51.46: “And lest your heart grow faint, and you fear the report heard in the land - for a report shall come one year, and after that, in another year a report shall come, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler -
51.47: therefore see, the days are coming that I shall bring punishment on the carved images of Baḇel, and all her land shall be put to shame, and all her slain fall in her midst.
51.48: “And the shamayim and the earth and all that is in them shall shout for joy over Baḇel, for the ravagers shall come to her from the north,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
51.49: As Baḇel is to fall for the slain of Yisra’ĕl, so for Baḇel the slain of all the earth shall fall.
51.50: You who have escaped the sword, go away! Do not stand still! Remember 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from afar, and let Yerushalayim come to your heart.
51.51: We are ashamed because we have heard reproach. Shame has covered our faces, for strangers have come into the miqdashim of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
51.52: “Therefore see, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “that I shall bring punishment on her carved images, while the wounded groan throughout all her land.
51.53: “Though Baḇel should mount up to the shamayim, and though she should make the height of her strength inaccessible, ravagers shall come to her from Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
51.54: Listen! A cry from Baḇel, and great destruction from the land of the Kasdites,
51.55: because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is ravaging Baḇel, and shall silence her loud voice. And her waves shall roar like great waters, the noise of their voice shall resound,
51.56: because the ravager shall come against her, against Baḇel, and her mighty men shall be captured. Every one of their bows shall be broken, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the Ĕl of recompense, He shall certainly repay.
51.57: “And I shall make her rulers drunk, and her wise men, her governors, and her deputies, and her mighty men. And they shall sleep a lasting sleep, and not awake,” declares the Meleḵ, whose Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts.
51.58: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “The broad walls of Baḇel are completely demolished, and her high gates are burned with fire, and peoples labor in vain, and the nations weary themselves for fire.”
51.59: The word that Yirmeyahu the naḇi commanded Serayah son of Nĕriyah, son of Maḥsĕyah, when he went with Tsiḏqiyahu the meleḵ of Yahuḏah to Baḇel in the fourth year of his reign. And Serayah was a quartermaster.
51.60: So Yirmeyahu wrote in a book all the evil that would come upon Baḇel, all these words which have been written concerning Baḇel.
51.61: And Yirmeyahu said to Serayah, “When you come to Baḇel and see it, and read all these words,
51.62: then you shall say, ‘O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You have spoken concerning this place to cut it off, so that none shall dwell in it, neither man nor beast, for it is a ruin forever.’
51.63: “And it shall be, when you have ended reading this book, that you shall tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of Perath,
51.64: and shall say, ‘So does Baḇel sink and not rise from the evil that I am bringing upon her, and they shall weary themselves.’ ” Thus far are the words of Yirmeyahu.

52.1: Tsiḏqiyahu was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Ḥamutal the daughter of Yirmeyahu of Liḇnah.
52.2: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that Yahoyaqim had done.
52.3: For through the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 this came to be against Yerushalayim and Yahuḏah, until He had cast them out from His presence. And Tsiḏqiyahu rebelled against the meleḵ of Baḇel.
52.4: And it came to be in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel and all his army came against Yerushalayim and encamped against it. And they built a siege wall against it all around.
52.5: And the city was under siege until the eleventh year of Meleḵ Tsiḏqiyahu.
52.6: On the ninth of the fourth month the scarcity of food was so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land.
52.7: Then the city wall was breached, and all the men of battle fled and went out of the city at night by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the meleḵ’s garden, while the Kasdites were near the city all around. And they went by way of the desert plain.
52.8: But the army of the Kasdites pursued the meleḵ, and they overtook Tsiḏqiyahu in the desert plains of Yeriḥo, and his entire army was scattered from him.
52.9: Then they captured the meleḵ and brought him up to the meleḵ of Baḇel at Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath, and he pronounced judgments on him.
52.10: And the meleḵ of Baḇel slew the sons of Tsiḏqiyahu before his eyes, and he also slew all the heads of Yahuḏah in Riḇlah.
52.11: And he put out the eyes of Tsiḏqiyahu. And the meleḵ of Baḇel bound him in bronze shackles, and took him to Baḇel, and put him in prison till the day of his death.
52.12: And on the tenth of the fifth month, which was the nineteenth year of meleḵ Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, who served the meleḵ of Baḇel, came to Yerushalayim,
52.13: and he burned the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the meleḵ’s house, and all the houses of Yerushalayim, and all the houses of the great men, he burned with fire.
52.14: And all the army of the Kasdites who were with the chief of the guard broke down all the walls of Yerushalayim all around.
52.15: And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, exiled some of the poor people, and the rest of the people who were left in the city, and the defectors who had gone over to the meleḵ of Baḇel, and the rest of the craftsmen.
52.16: But Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, left some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and farmers.
52.17: And the Kasdites broke the bronze columns that were in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and brought all their bronze to Baḇel.
52.18: They also took away the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the ladles, and all the bronze utensils with which they served,
52.19: and the basins, and the fire holders, and the bowls, and the pots, and the lampstands, and the ladles, and the cups, whatever was of solid gold and whatever was of solid silver, the chief of the guard took.
52.20: The two columns, one sea, the twelve bronze bulls which were under it, and the stands, which Meleḵ Shelomoh had made for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.
52.21: As for the columns, the height of one column was eighteen ammah, and its circumference was twelve ammah, and its thickness was four etsba’oth, hollow.
52.22: And a capital of bronze was on it. And the height of one capital was five ammah, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. And the second column, with pomegranates was the same.
52.23: And there were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides. All the pomegranates on the network were one hundred, all around.
52.24: And the chief of the guard took Serayah the chief kohĕn, and Tsephanyah the second kohĕn, and the three doorkeepers.
52.25: And from the city he took one eunuch who was in charge of the men of battle, and seven men who saw the meleḵ’s face, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
52.26: And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, took these and brought them to the meleḵ of Baḇel at Riḇlah,
52.27: and the meleḵ of Baḇel smote them and put them to death at Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath. Thus Yahuḏah was exiled from its own land.
52.28: These are the people whom Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar exiled: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Yahuḏim;
52.29: in the eighteenth year of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar he exiled from Yerushalayim eight hundred and thirty-two beings;
52.30: in the twenty-third year of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, exiled of the Yahuḏim seven hundred and forty-five beings. All the beings were four thousand six hundred.
52.31: And it came to be in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Yahoyaḵin meleḵ of Yahuḏah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth of the month, that Ewil-Meroḏaḵ meleḵ of Baḇel, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Yahoyaḵin meleḵ of Yahuḏah and brought him out of prison,
52.32: and spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above those of the melaḵim who were with him in Baḇel.
52.33: So he changed his prison garments, and he ate bread continually before the meleḵ all the days of his life.
52.34: And as for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him by the meleḵ of Baḇel, a portion for each day until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

6.1: “O children of Binyamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Yerushalayim! Blow the ram’s horn in Teqowa, and put up a signal-fire in Bĕyth ha’Kkerem, for evil has been seen from the north, and great destruction.
6.2: “I shall cut off the lovely and delicate one, the daughter of Tsiyon.
6.3: “The shepherds with their flocks shall come to her, they shall pitch their tents against her all around. They shall pasture, each one in his own place.”
6.4: “Declare battle against her. Arise, and let us go up at noon. Woe to us, for the day goes away, for the shadows of the evening are lengthening.
6.5: “Arise, and let us go by night, and let us destroy her palaces.”
6.6: For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “Cut down her trees, and cast up a siege mound against Yerushalayim. She is the city to be punished, in whose midst there is only oppression.
6.7: “As a well flows with water, so she flows with her evil. Violence and destruction are heard in her. Before Me continually are suffering and smiting.
6.8: “Be instructed, O Yerushalayim, lest My being be torn from you, lest I make you a waste, a land not inhabited.”
6.9: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “Let them thoroughly glean as a vine the remnant of Yisra’ĕl; pass your hand again over the branches like a grape-gatherer.”
6.10: To whom shall I speak and give warning, so that they hear? See, their ear is uncircumcised, and they are unable to listen. See, the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is a reproach to them, they do not delight in it.
6.11: Therefore I am filled with the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. I have become weary of containing it. “Pour it out on the children outside, and on the company of young men together, for even husband and wife shall be taken, the aged and the very old.
6.12: “And their houses shall be turned over to others, fields and wives together. For I shall stretch out My hand against the inhabitants of the land,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.13: “For from the least of them even to the greatest of them, they are all greedy for gain. And from the naḇi even to the kohĕn, all act falsely.
6.14: “And they heal the breach of My people slightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.
6.15: “Were they ashamed when they had done abomination? No! They were not at all ashamed, nor did they know how to blush. Therefore they shall fall among those who fall. They shall stumble at the time I visit them,” said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.16: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, where the good way is, and walk in it; and find rest for yourselves. But they said, ‘We do not walk.’
6.17: “And I raised up watchmen over you, ‘Listen to the sound of the ram’s horn!’ But they said, ‘We do not listen.’
6.18: “Therefore hear, you nations, and know, O congregation, what is upon them!
6.19: “Hear, O earth! See, I am bringing evil upon this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not listened to My Words, nor My Torah - and they rejected it.
6.20: “What need have I of frankincense from Sheḇa, and sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your slaughterings have not been sweet to Me.”
6.21: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, I am laying stumbling-blocks before this people. And the fathers and the sons together shall stumble on them, the neighbor and his friend shall perish.”
6.22: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, a people shall come from the land of the north, and a great nation is stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth,
6.23: they seize bow and spear, they are cruel and have no compassion, their voice roars like the sea. And they ride on horses, put in array as a man for battle against you, O daughter of Tsiyon.”
6.24: We have heard the report of it, our hands grow weak. Distress has taken hold of us, pain as of a woman in labor.
6.25: Do not go out into the field, nor walk by the way. Because of the sword of the enemy, fear is on every side.
6.26: O daughter of my people, gird on sackcloth, and roll about in ashes! Make mourning as for an only son, most bitter lamentation because suddenly the ravager shall come upon us.
6.27: “I have made you a trier and a stronghold among My people, so that you know, and shall try their way.
6.28: “All of them are rebels of rebels, walking as slanderers. They are bronze and iron, all of them are corrupters.
6.29: “The bellows have burned, the lead has been consumed by fire. The refiner has refined in vain, for those who are evil have not been separated.
6.30: “They shall call them rejected silver, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has rejected them.”

7.1: The word that came to Yirmeyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
7.2: “Stand in the gate of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and you shall proclaim there this word, and shall say, ‘Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all you of Yahuḏah who enter in at these gates to bow before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!’ ”
7.3: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Make your ways and your deeds good, then I let you dwell in this place.
7.4: “Do not trust in these false words, saying, ‘This is the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!’
7.5: “For if you truly make your ways and your deeds good, if you truly do right-ruling between a man and his neighbor,
7.6: if you do not oppress the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, or walk after other mighty ones to your own evil,
7.7: then I shall let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers forever and ever.
7.8: “See, you are trusting in false words, which do not profit -
7.9: stealing, murdering, and committing adultery, and swearing falsely, and burning incense to Ba’al, and walking after other mighty ones you have not known.
7.10: “And you came and stood before Me in this house which is called by My Name, and said, ‘We have been delivered’ - in order to do all these abominations!
7.11: “Has this house, which is called by My Name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Look, I, even I Myself have seen it,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.12: “But go now to My place at Shiloh, where I put My Name at the first, and see what I did to it because of the evil of My people Yisra’ĕl.
7.13: “And now, because you have done all these works,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “and I spoke to you, rising up early and speaking, but you did not hear, and I called you, but you did not answer,
7.14: “I shall also do to this house, which is called by My Name, in which you trust, and to this place which I gave to you and your fathers, as I did to Shiloh.
7.15: “And I shall cast you out of My presence, as I have cast out all your brothers, all the seed of Ephrayim.
7.16: “And you, do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or prayer for them, nor make intercession to Me, for I do not hear you.
7.17: “Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Yahuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim?
7.18: “The children are gathering wood, the fathers are lighting the fire, and the women are kneading their dough, to make cakes for the queen of the shamayim, and to pour out drink offerings to other mighty ones, to provoke Me.
7.19: “Is it Me they are provoking?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “Is it not themselves - unto the shame of their own faces?”
7.20: Therefore, thus said Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, My displeasure and My wrath is poured out on this place, on man and on beast, and on the trees of the field and on the fruit of the ground. And it shall burn and not be quenched.”
7.21: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Add your burnt offerings to your slaughterings and eat meat.
7.22: “For I did not speak to your fathers, or command them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, about matters of burnt offerings or slaughterings.
7.23: “But this Word I commanded them, saying, ‘Obey My voice, and I shall be your Elohim, and you be My people. And walk in all the Ways that I have commanded you, so that it be well with you.’
7.24: “But they did not obey or incline their ear, but walked in the counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart, and went backward and not forward.
7.25: “From the day that your fathers came out of the land of Mitsrayim until this day, I have even sent to you all My servants the neḇi’im, daily rising up early and sending them.
7.26: “But they did not obey Me or incline their ear, but stiffened their neck. They did evil, more than their fathers.
7.27: “And you shall speak all these words to them, though they do not listen to you. And you shall also call to them, though they do not answer you.
7.28: “But you shall say to them, ‘This is a nation that did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, nor did they accept instruction. Truth has perished and has been cut off from their mouth.
7.29: ‘Cut off your hair and throw it away, and take up a lamentation on the bare heights, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.’
7.30: “For the children of Yahuḏah have done what is evil in My eyes,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “They have put their abominations in the House which is called by My Name, to defile it.
7.31: “And they have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which I did not command, nor did it come into My heart.
7.32: “Therefore see, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when it shall no longer be called Topheth, or the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter, for they shall bury in Topheth until no room is left.
7.33: “And the corpses of this people shall be food for the birds of the shamayim and for the beasts of the earth, with none to frighten them away.
7.34: “And in the cities of Yahuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim I shall make to cease the voice of rejoicing and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride. For the land shall become a waste!

8.1: “At that time,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “they shall bring the bones of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah, and the bones of its heads, and the bones of the kohenim, and the bones of the neḇi’im, and the bones of the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, out of their graves,
8.2: and shall spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of the heavens, which they have loved and which they have served and after which they have walked, which they have sought, and to which they have bowed themselves. They shall not be gathered nor buried, they shall be for dung on the face of the earth.
8.3: “And death shall be preferred to life by all the rest of those who remain of this evil people, who remain in all the places where I have driven them,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts.
8.4: “And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Would they fall, and not rise? Does one turn away and not return?
8.5: “Why then has this people, Yerushalayim, turned away in a continual backsliding? They seize upon deceit, they refuse to turn back.
8.6: “I have listened and heard - they do not speak right. No man has repented of his evil, saying, ‘What have I done?’ They all turned to their own course, like a horse rushing into battle.
8.7: “Even a stork in the shamayim knows her appointed times. And a turtledove, and a swallow, and a thrush guard the time of their coming. But My people do not know the Right-Ruling of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.8: “How do you say, ‘We are wise, and the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with us’? But look, the false pen of the scribe has worked falsehood.
8.9: “The wise shall be put to shame, they shall be broken down and caught. See, they have rejected the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, so what wisdom do they have?
8.10: “Therefore I give their wives to others, and their fields to possessing ones. For from the least even to the greatest, they are all greedy for gain. From the naḇi to the kohĕn, all act falsely.
8.11: “And they heal the breach of the daughter of My people slightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace!’ when there is no peace.
8.12: “Were they ashamed when they had done abomination? No! They were not at all ashamed, nor did they know how to blush. So they shall fall among those who fall. They shall stumble in the time of their visitation,” said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.13: “I shall snatch them away,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “There are no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf has faded. And what I gave them shall pass away from them.” ’ ”
8.14: Why are we sitting still? Gather yourselves, and let us go into the walled cities, and let us be silent there. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim has let us perish and given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.15: We looked for peace, but there was no good; for a time of healing, but see - fear!
8.16: The snorting of his horses was heard from Dan. All the land shook at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones. They came and devoured the land and all that fills it, the city and those who dwell in it.
8.17: “For look, I am sending among you serpents, adders, which have no enchanter, and they shall bite you,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.18: When in grief I would seek comfort; my heart is sick within me.
8.19: Observe! The voice, the cry of the daughter of my people from a distant land, “Is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 not in Tsiyon? Is her Meleḵ not in her?” “Why have they provoked Me with their carved images, and with foreign worthlessnesses?”
8.20: “The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we have not been saved!”
8.21: For the breach of the daughter of my people I have been broken. I have grown sad; astonishment has seized me.
8.22: Is there no balm in Gil’aḏ, is there no healer there? Why has the healing of the daughter of my people not come?

9.1: Oh, that my head were waters, and my eyes a fountain of tears, and I would weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
9.2: Oh, that I had in the wilderness lodging place for wayfaring men, and I would leave my people, and go from them! For they are all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.
9.3: “And they bend their tongue like a bow. Falsehood, and not truth, prevails on the earth. For they proceed from evil to evil, and they have not known Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.4: “Let everyone beware of his neighbor and not trust any brother. For every brother catches by the heel, and every neighbor walks with slanderers.
9.5: “And everyone deceives his neighbor, and no one speaks the truth. They have taught their tongue to speak falsehood, and have wearied themselves to do wickedly.
9.6: “You live in the midst of deceit; through deceit they have refused to know Me,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.7: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “See, I shall refine them, and shall try them, for what shall I do because of the daughter of My people?
9.8: “Their tongue is a slaying arrow. It speaks deceit - speaks peaceably to his neighbor with his mouth, but in his heart he makes his ambush.
9.9: “Would I not punish them for this?” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “Would I not revenge Myself on such a nation as this?”
9.10: “I shall take up a weeping and wailing for the mountains, and for the pastures of the wilderness a lamentation, because they have been burned up, without any passing over, nor has the voice of cattle been heard. Both the birds of the shamayim and the beasts have fled, they have gone.
9.11: “And I shall make Yerushalayim a heap of ruins, a habitation for jackals; and the cities of Yahuḏah I shall make a waste, without an inhabitant.”
9.12: Who is the wise man, that he understands this? And to whom has the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoken, that he declares it? Why has the land perished, has it been burned up like a wilderness, with none passing through?
9.13: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 says, “Because they have forsaken My Torah which I put before them, and have not obeyed My voice, nor walked according to it,
9.14: but they have walked according to the stubbornness of their own heart and after the Ba’als, which their fathers had taught them.”
9.15: Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “See, I am making this people eat wormwood, and I shall make them drink poisoned water.
9.16: “And I shall scatter them among the gentiles, whom neither they nor their fathers have known. And I shall send a sword after them until I have consumed them.”
9.17: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “Discern! And call for the mourning women, that they come. And send for the wise women, that they come.
9.18: “And let them hasten and take up a wailing for us, and let our eyes run with tears and our eyelids gush with water.
9.19: “For a voice of wailing is heard from Tsiyon, ‘How we are ravaged! We are greatly ashamed, because we have forsaken the land, because we have been thrown out of our dwellings.’ ”
9.20: But hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O women, and let your ear receive the word of His mouth. And teach your daughters wailing, and each one her neighbor a lamentation.
9.21: For death has come through our windows, has entered our palaces, cutting off the children from the streets, and the young men from the squares.
9.22: Speak, “Thus declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘The corpses of men shall fall as dung on the face of the field, like cuttings after the reaper, with none to gather them.’ ”
9.23: Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Let not the wise boast in his wisdom, let not the mighty boast in his might, nor let the rich boast in his riches,
9.24: but let him who boasts boast of this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, doing kindness, right-ruling, and righteousness in the earth. For in these I delight,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.25: “See, the days are coming,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “when I shall punish all circumcised with the uncircumcised -
9.26: “Mitsrayim, and Yahuḏah, and Eḏom, and the children of Ammon, and Mo’aḇ, and all those trimmed on the edges, who dwell in the wilderness. For all the gentiles are uncircumcised, and all the house of Yisra’ĕl are uncircumcised in heart!”
